name: The Fool
essence: A first step taken with open eyes and a light pack.
figure: A traveller in a green jacket strides to the lip of a cliff, face tilted to the sun, red scarf streaming behind and a small pack on their back. A white-and-tan dog bounds at their heels. This is the beginner in all of us: unproven, unburdened and willing to find out.

symbols.meaning: The point where planning stops and experience begins; the drop is real, and so is the view.
Instinct and loyal company, keeping pace and barking when your attention drifts too far.
Everything carried over from before fits on one back; beginning takes less than you think.
Enthusiasm caught by the wind, a bright streak of appetite for whatever comes next.

upright.short: Beginnings, curiosity and taking a thoughtful leap.
upright.meaning: The Fool marks the moment before you know how something turns out. It favours saying yes to a new road while you are still a beginner, trusting that you can learn as you walk. It also asks that the leap be thoughtful: look at the ground, then step.
upright.love: Meet someone new, or a familiar partner, without the script of what happened last time.
upright.work: Try the project you feel underqualified for and let yourself ask the obvious questions.
upright.self: Give yourself permission to be new at something and to enjoy not being the expert.
upright.advice: Take one small, reversible step toward the thing that keeps tugging at you.

reversed.short: Notice where hesitation or haste is standing in for a thoughtful first step.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the Fool's leap stalls or goes wild. You may be circling the edge, waiting to feel completely ready, or jumping to escape rather than to explore. Either way the missing piece is the same: an honest look at what you are stepping into and why.
reversed.love: Ask whether you are holding back out of old caution or rushing in to avoid your own company.
reversed.work: A plan that keeps being postponed may need a smaller first version rather than more courage.
reversed.self: Be gentle with the part of you that wants a guarantee before it moves; nobody is handed one.
reversed.advice: Name the one fact you would want to know first, find it out, and only then decide.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is thought and movement; here it is the open sky the traveller walks out into.

astrology.name: Uranus
astrology.gloss: A modern pairing for sudden change and independence; older tables give the Fool Air alone.

number.gloss: Zero is unnumbered potential, the blank page before any counting has begun.

questions: Where in your life are you being invited to begin before you feel ready?
What would you pack, and what would you gladly leave behind, for a fresh start?

name: The Magician
essence: Everything you need is already on the table.
figure: A robed figure in red, patterned with stars, lifts a wand toward a blazing point of light and points the other hand down at a table. On the cloth lie a golden cup, a sword and a star-stamped disc. This is the maker: the one who connects an idea overhead to the materials at hand.

symbols.meaning: One hand reaches for inspiration, the other directs it to the table: ideas made practical.
The four suits laid out as tools: feeling, thought, resources and drive, all within reach.
Full attention, lit like a spotlight; skill begins with where you choose to look.
Desire and clear intention growing side by side around the work.

upright.short: Resourcefulness: turn the skills you already have into action.
upright.meaning: The Magician is about agency. You have more tools than you are using, and this card points at them one by one. It favours action that joins a clear intention to a concrete skill: say what you mean to make, pick up the first tool, and begin while your focus is sharp.
upright.love: Say plainly what you want and show it through small, deliberate acts rather than hints.
upright.work: List the skills and contacts you already have; the next move is probably hiding in that inventory.
upright.self: Notice how capable you are when your attention is gathered in one place instead of scattered.
upright.advice: Choose one tool you already own and use it today for the thing you keep meaning to start.

reversed.short: Check whether your skill is scattered, unused or bent toward managing impressions.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the tools stay on the table. Talent goes unused because you doubt it, or energy sprays in ten directions and nothing gets finished. The card can also flag cleverness used to steer people rather than to make something. Returning to one honest aim steadies the hands.
reversed.love: Charm is working overtime if you are performing interest instead of sharing what is true for you.
reversed.work: Talking about the plan has become a substitute for doing it; shrink the task until you can start.
reversed.self: Doubt is telling you that you lack something, yet the evidence of your past work says otherwise.
reversed.advice: Finish one small thing before opening anything new, and be straight about your motives.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air here is the quick, connecting mind that turns an idea into a clear instruction.

astrology.name: Mercury
astrology.gloss: Mercury is the planet of skill, speech and trade: the messenger who makes things move.

number.gloss: One is the single point of will: a beginning that has decided what it is for.

questions: Which of your abilities are you treating as ordinary when it is actually your sharpest tool?
What would you make this week if you trusted that you already had enough to begin?

name: The High Priestess
essence: The quiet knowledge that waits beneath the noise.
figure: A veiled woman sits between two pale pillars under a crescent moon, chin resting on her hand, an open book of star charts on the table before her. She looks straight at you and says nothing. She is the keeper of what is known but not yet spoken: intuition, memory and the inner life.

symbols.meaning: A threshold between the outer world and the inner one; she sits exactly at the doorway.
Knowledge that is available but must be read slowly, in your own time, by your own light.
Understanding that arrives in phases, partly lit, asking for patience rather than proof.
Some things are held back on purpose; privacy and mystery have their own dignity.
The calm surface of feeling that reflects clearly only when nothing is stirred.

upright.short: Listen closely to intuition and what remains unsaid.
upright.meaning: The High Priestess asks you to stop gathering opinions and listen inward. Something is already understood at a level below words: a hunch, a pattern, a detail that keeps returning. The card favours waiting, watching and reading between the lines over forcing an answer into the open.
upright.love: Pay attention to what is communicated in tone, timing and silence as well as in words.
upright.work: Hold your plan a little longer and observe; the room is telling you more than the agenda is.
upright.self: Make quiet time ordinary, so that your own signal has a chance to be heard above everyone else's.
upright.advice: Write down the hunch you keep dismissing and treat it as information worth checking.

reversed.short: Ask what you already sense but keep overriding, hiding or waiting for others to confirm.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the inner voice is muffled. You may be overruling a clear instinct because it is inconvenient, or leaning so far into privacy that people cannot reach you. Unspoken things pile up on both sides. A little honest disclosure, to yourself first, lets the water settle again.
reversed.love: Something unsaid is doing a lot of talking; consider which silence protects and which only hides.
reversed.work: Information is being held back, perhaps by you; ask the direct question before assuming.
reversed.self: Constant input from screens and voices is crowding out your own read on things.
reversed.advice: Spend ten quiet minutes without input, then note the first thing you know to be true.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is feeling and reflection; here it is deep, still and able to mirror what is above.

astrology.name: Moon
astrology.gloss: The Moon rules instinct, memory and tides: what moves you before you have reasons.

number.gloss: Two is the pause between opposites, where you hold both sides before choosing.

questions: What do you know about your situation that you have not yet admitted out loud?
Where would waiting and watching serve you better than pushing for an answer?

name: The Empress
essence: Abundance that comes from tending, not from rushing.
figure: A woman crowned with stars reclines on a stone seat in a floral gown, one hand resting on a split pomegranate, with fruit trees, grapes and blossom crowding in on every side. She is entirely at ease. She stands for the nurturing, creative force that makes things grow by giving them time and care.

symbols.meaning: Ripeness and creative fruitfulness: many seeds held inside one generous form.
Care that follows a natural calendar; growth has seasons and cannot be hurried.
Pleasure in the senses: colour, texture and beauty treated as nourishment, not luxury.
Proof of patient tending, where what was looked after now gives back freely.

upright.short: Nurture creativity, care and the things that need time to grow.
upright.meaning: The Empress is the card of things that thrive because someone looks after them. It favours patience, pleasure and practical care: feeding a project, a body, a friendship or a garden until it flourishes. Her question is less about what you can produce and more about what you are willing to tend.
upright.love: Affection shows up as care you can feel: warmth, good food, time and unhurried attention.
upright.work: A creative idea is ready to be developed; protect the slow middle stage where it puts on weight.
upright.self: Let yourself enjoy comfort and beauty without having to earn them first.
upright.advice: Pick one thing that is growing and give it steady attention instead of a burst of effort.

reversed.short: See where care has turned into smothering, or where your own needs go untended.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the garden is out of balance. You may be pouring care into everyone else while your own ground dries out, or holding something so closely that it cannot grow on its own. Creativity can feel blocked for the same reason. Rest and a little room on both sides bring the green back.
reversed.love: Looking after someone has tipped into managing them; ask what they would like, then believe the answer.
reversed.work: An idea is being overworked or underfed; step back and check what it actually needs from you.
reversed.self: You are last on your own list, and tiredness is beginning to pass itself off as generosity.
reversed.advice: Do one nourishing thing purely for yourself before you look after anyone else today.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is body, soil and the senses; here it is rich ground that rewards steady care.

astrology.name: Venus
astrology.gloss: Venus governs love, beauty and pleasure: what draws you close and makes life sweet.

number.gloss: Three is growth: two things meet and something new comes into being between them.

questions: What in your life is asking for patient tending rather than a quick result?
How do you receive care, and how easily do you allow yourself to accept it?

name: The Emperor
essence: Structure that protects what matters.
figure: A bearded ruler in a red cloak sits squarely on a stone throne carved with eagles, a golden sceptre planted beside him and a snow-capped mountain rising behind. Nothing about the posture is hurried. He stands for order, authority and the steadying work of setting rules that hold.

symbols.meaning: Stability built to last: decisions made from a settled seat instead of a passing mood.
A wide, high view; leadership that watches the whole territory and not only the next step.
Authority held upright and in plain sight, with responsibility attached to it.
Firm limits and long endurance, the kind of backdrop that does not move when pushed.

upright.short: Give your ambition structure, boundaries and steady leadership.
upright.meaning: The Emperor brings shape to ambition. It favours plans, limits and clear lines of responsibility: deciding who does what, by when, and what is not up for negotiation. Good authority here is protective. It creates the conditions in which other people, and your own goals, can rely on you.
upright.love: Reliability is its own kind of romance; keep your word and say clearly where your limits are.
upright.work: Take the lead by setting the framework: priorities, roles and a schedule people can trust.
upright.self: A firmer routine could steady you, giving energy somewhere dependable to go.
upright.advice: Write down one rule for yourself that protects your priorities, and keep it for a week.

reversed.short: Look at where control has grown rigid, or where needed structure is missing.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the throne is either gripped too hard or left empty. Rules become rigid, orders replace conversation and control stands in for confidence. The opposite also appears: no plan, no limits and a wish that someone else would decide. Flexible firmness, discussed openly, restores balance.
reversed.love: A contest over who is in charge is crowding out tenderness; try asking instead of instructing.
reversed.work: Micromanaging, or a boss who does, is slowing things down; agree the outcome and loosen the method.
reversed.self: Your inner taskmaster is loud at the moment, or missing altogether; neither is the same as discipline.
reversed.advice: Loosen one rule that no longer serves anyone, or set the one boundary you keep avoiding.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is will and initiative; here it is disciplined into a steady, governing flame.

astrology.name: Aries
astrology.gloss: Aries is the first sign: the pioneer who steps forward and takes charge.

number.gloss: Four is the square: walls, corners and foundations that make a thing stable.

questions: Where would a clear boundary make your life simpler and kinder at the same time?
What kind of authority do you respect, and do you practise it yourself?

name: The Hierophant
essence: Wisdom handed down, and the choice of what to keep.
figure: A grey-bearded teacher in red and white vestments stands in an archway holding two golden keys crossed at his chest, while three listeners look up at him with their backs to us. He stands for tradition, shared belief and learning passed from one generation to the next.

symbols.meaning: Access to knowledge that someone else has already unlocked and is willing to pass on.
Learning in company: questions asked aloud and answers heard together.
An institution or tradition as a doorway that frames how you enter and what you see.
Peaceable common ground, the values a community agrees to live by.

upright.short: Consider tradition, trusted guidance and which rules serve you.
upright.meaning: The Hierophant points to teachers, institutions and well-worn paths. It favours learning the established way before improvising, seeking out a mentor, or joining something larger than yourself. The card also invites discernment: a tradition earns its place by helping you live well.
upright.love: Shared values, rituals and commitments give a relationship its spine; talk about the ones you want.
upright.work: Find the person who has done this before and ask how; proven methods save you years.
upright.self: A practice you return to regularly, whatever its source, can hold you when motivation dips.
upright.advice: Ask one experienced person for guidance and listen all the way to the end of the answer.

reversed.short: Question inherited rules, and notice if rebellion has become its own orthodoxy.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the keys do not fit the lock. Rules you inherited may no longer match what you believe, and following them out of habit feels hollow. Equally, rejecting every convention on principle can become a rigid creed of its own. Keep what holds meaning, release the rest, and say why.
reversed.love: Expectations from family or culture may be louder than what the two of you truly want.
reversed.work: The standard procedure is being followed for its own sake; propose the better way, with reasons.
reversed.self: You are allowed to outgrow a belief and still respect the people who taught it to you.
reversed.advice: Pick one rule you follow automatically and decide, on purpose, whether it still earns its keep.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is the durable and practical; here it is custom worn smooth by long use.

astrology.name: Taurus
astrology.gloss: Taurus is steady and loyal: it values what lasts and builds slowly on it.

number.gloss: Five is the teacher's number here: a centre point that the other four gather around.

questions: Which traditions do you keep because they nourish you, and which out of habit?
Who has been a true teacher to you, and what did they pass on that you still use?

name: The Lovers
essence: A choice made with the whole heart.
figure: Two people sit close together on a stone bench in a walled garden in full bloom, turned toward each other and holding one another's gaze beneath a wide, rayed sun. They stand for union and for the deeper matter beneath it: choosing who and what you align yourself with.

symbols.meaning: Mutual recognition: being seen clearly and choosing to stay present anyway.
Openness and honesty; nothing in this meeting needs to be kept in shadow.
What flourishes when two things are well matched and both are cared for.
A decision to sit down together, a commitment with some weight to it.

upright.short: Choose in alignment with your values and communicate honestly.
upright.meaning: The Lovers is a card of meaningful choice. It can speak of romance, yet its wider subject is harmony between what you value and what you do. It favours decisions made openly, with your eyes on the other person or the path in front of you, and with honest words about what you want.
upright.love: Closeness deepens when both of you say what you actually want instead of what sounds agreeable.
upright.work: Choose the option that fits your principles, even when another one looks better on paper.
upright.self: Notice where your actions and your values are in step; that match is what integrity feels like.
upright.advice: State your real preference in one clear sentence to the person it most concerns.

reversed.short: Find where your choices and values have drifted apart, and say so honestly.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, something is out of tune. A choice is being dodged, a relationship is running on mixed messages, or you are acting against your own values to keep the peace. The discomfort is useful information. Naming the gap honestly, without blame, is usually the first step back into harmony.
reversed.love: One of you may be keeping quiet to avoid friction, and the distance that creates is growing.
reversed.work: You have said yes to something that sits badly with you; revisit the terms before resentment sets in.
reversed.self: An inner tug-of-war eases once you admit which side you have truly been favouring.
reversed.advice: Write down the choice you are avoiding and what each option would say about your values.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is conversation and thought; here it is the honest exchange that lets two minds meet.

astrology.name: Gemini
astrology.gloss: Gemini is the sign of the twins: dialogue, curiosity and seeing two sides at once.

number.gloss: Six is harmony and reciprocity, a balanced exchange where giving and receiving agree.

questions: What would you choose if you were being completely honest about what matters to you?
Where are you saying one thing and doing another, and what would close that gap?

name: The Chariot
essence: Two forces, one direction, held by a steady hand.
figure: A driver in a laurel wreath and red cape stands in a gilded chariot, reins in both hands, drawn by a black panther and a white lioness in striped headdresses that pull shoulder to shoulder through the dust. This is the will in motion: someone who has harnessed opposing drives and chosen where to go.

symbols.meaning: Opposing impulses, such as caution and appetite, made to pull the same way.
Control that guides rather than fights; a light, constant hand on what drives you.
A clear purpose fixed at the front, the thing every effort is steered toward.
Victory earned through discipline and persistence more than through luck.

upright.short: Bring competing impulses together and choose a clear direction.
upright.meaning: The Chariot is about moving forward on purpose. Competing wants do not disappear; they are yoked together and pointed somewhere. The card favours commitment, focus and the confidence to steer. Progress comes from holding your line while staying alert to the road, not from speed alone.
upright.love: Decide together where this is heading; shared direction matters more than matching moods.
upright.work: Pick the single objective that counts and organise your effort around reaching it.
upright.self: You can feel two things at once and still act; let the calmer hand hold the reins.
upright.advice: Choose your destination for this month and decline one thing that leads away from it.

reversed.short: Notice where you are pulled two ways, forcing the pace or drifting off course.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the panther and the lioness pull apart. You may be pushing hard with no agreed destination, or stuck because part of you wants to go and part of you wants to stay. Sheer force makes the wheels spin. Slowing down long enough to settle the inner disagreement gets you moving again.
reversed.love: You and a partner may be steering toward different futures without having said so aloud.
reversed.work: Effort is high and progress is low; the goal itself may need redefining before you push further.
reversed.self: Willpower is being used to override a part of you that deserves a hearing first.
reversed.advice: Stop, name the two things you want that conflict, and decide which one leads this time.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is feeling; here it is strong emotion channelled so it carries you forward.

astrology.name: Cancer
astrology.gloss: Cancer is protective and tenacious: a soft interior carried inside sturdy armour.

number.gloss: Seven is the test of resolve, where a plan meets resistance and has to prove itself.

questions: What are the two forces pulling at you, and what would it look like to harness both?
Where are you going, and did you choose that destination or simply inherit it?

name: Strength
essence: Gentleness that is stronger than force.
figure: A woman with flowers in her hair rests her cheek against the mane of a great lion, one hand at its jaw, and the animal's eyes are closed in calm. No chain or whip is anywhere in sight. She stands for courage of the quiet kind: patience, compassion and mastery of your own wilder impulses.

symbols.meaning: Raw instinct, anger or appetite: powerful, alive and willing to settle when met with respect.
Influence through touch and trust, the opposite of gripping or forcing.
Softness worn openly, with no sense that tenderness needs to be hidden to be safe.
Steady inner warmth, the vitality that makes patience possible.

upright.short: Meet difficulty with patient courage rather than force.
upright.meaning: Strength shows power that does not need to prove itself. It favours meeting a difficult person, feeling or task with calm persistence, staying close to what scares you until it eases. The lion is not defeated here; it is befriended. That is the harder and more lasting kind of bravery.
upright.love: Stay kind in a hard conversation; warmth lowers defences that pressure only raises.
upright.work: Handle the tense situation with composure and persistence instead of matching its volume.
upright.self: Speak to your own anger or craving as you would to a large animal you respect: calmly and near.
upright.advice: When you feel the urge to push, soften your voice and hold your position a moment longer.

reversed.short: Notice self-doubt or forcefulness where calm, patient courage is needed.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the bond between hand and lion slips. You may doubt your ability to cope, or swing the other way and try to overpower a situation that needs patience. Temper frays and energy runs low. Strength returns when you treat yourself with the same gentleness the card asks you to show others.
reversed.love: Harsh words or silent withdrawal are standing in for the vulnerable thing you could say instead.
reversed.work: Powering through on willpower alone is wearing you down; ask what support would make this bearable.
reversed.self: Your inner critic has grabbed the whip, and you are more tired than you have admitted.
reversed.advice: Rest first, then return to the hard thing with half the force and twice the patience.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is vitality and heart; here it burns warm and steady instead of flaring up.

astrology.name: Leo
astrology.gloss: Leo is the lion's sign: courage, pride and a generous, loyal heart.

number.gloss: Eight is sustained power, the figure-of-eight rhythm of effort renewed again and again.

questions: What in you needs taming with kindness and not with force?
Where could staying calm and close achieve more than pushing harder?

name: The Hermit
essence: A single lamp, held up in the quiet.
figure: A hooded elder with a grey beard climbs a rocky height at night, a walking staff in one hand and a glowing lantern raised in the other, with a full moon and a river valley far below. He stands for solitude chosen on purpose: stepping away to think, and carrying your own light.

symbols.meaning: Your own understanding: it lights only the next few steps, and that is enough to go on.
Experience to lean on, earned the slow way over rough ground.
Distance from the crowd that makes a wider, calmer view possible.
Deliberate withdrawal, attention turned inward and away from display.

upright.short: Step back from noise to find your own considered answer.
upright.meaning: The Hermit favours time alone with a question. Away from other people's opinions, you can hear what you think and see what you have learned. This is retreat with a purpose, not loneliness: you step back in order to return clearer, and perhaps to light the way for someone else.
upright.love: A little space, taken kindly, can help you understand what you feel and want to offer.
upright.work: Do the deep, uninterrupted thinking the problem needs before you ask for more input.
upright.self: Treat time on your own as a meeting with someone whose view you value.
upright.advice: Block out an hour with no company and no screen, and take your question for a walk.

reversed.short: Ask whether solitude has become isolation, or busyness is keeping reflection away.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the retreat has gone on too long or has not been allowed at all. You may be hiding from people who would welcome you, or filling every hour so that you never have to sit with your own thoughts. The lantern needs both: quiet to tend the flame and company to share it with.
reversed.love: Withdrawing to protect yourself is also keeping out the closeness you would like.
reversed.work: Working alone on everything is a habit, not a necessity; let someone see the draft.
reversed.self: Notice whether you are alone because it restores you or because reaching out feels risky.
reversed.advice: Send one message to a person you trust and tell them something true about your week.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is the practical and careful; here it is the patient step-by-step of a long climb.

astrology.name: Virgo
astrology.gloss: Virgo is thoughtful and discerning: it refines, studies and quietly serves.

number.gloss: Nine is near-completion, the last stretch where you gather what the journey has taught.

questions: What question would you take with you if you had a whole day alone to think?
Is your current distance from others restoring you or protecting you from something?

name: Wheel of Fortune
essence: Everything turns; your part is how you meet the turning.
figure: A great golden wheel with a sun at its hub hangs among clouds, its segments filled with blossom, summer leaves, autumn colour, snowflakes and phases of the moon. A winged figure, an eagle, a bull and a lion keep watch around the rim. It stands for cycles, chance and the changing seasons of a life.

symbols.meaning: Spring, summer, autumn and winter on one rim: every phase leads into the next.
A still centre; the closer you stand to your own middle, the less the spin throws you.
Angel, eagle, bull and lion: fixed points that stay steady while the wheel moves.
The thread of your own story, running through every rise and dip of the rim.

upright.short: Circumstances shift; respond to change without assuming control of it.
upright.meaning: The Wheel of Fortune reminds you that circumstances move. What is up comes down and what is stuck begins to shift, often for reasons outside your control. The card favours flexibility and good timing: ride the turn that is happening, stay centred, and avoid taking luck too personally.
upright.love: Relationships have seasons; meet the present one as it is instead of comparing it with an earlier one.
upright.work: Conditions are shifting; stay light on your feet and ready to use an opening when it appears.
upright.self: Remember a time things changed unexpectedly and you adapted; that capacity is still yours.
upright.advice: Sort today's worries into what you can influence and what you can only respond to.

reversed.short: Notice resistance to a change already under way, or a pattern that keeps repeating.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the wheel feels jammed or seems to bring the same thing round again. You may be bracing against a change that has already begun, or blaming luck for a loop that your own habits help to turn. Loosening your grip, and changing one small input, lets the rim move once more.
reversed.love: The same argument returning is a signal that the underlying pattern wants attention.
reversed.work: A setback is tempting you to wait for conditions to improve; adjust the one thing in your hands.
reversed.self: Telling yourself you are simply unlucky can hide the choices that are still available.
reversed.advice: Identify one repeating pattern and change a single step in how you usually respond.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is energy in motion; here it is the momentum that keeps the wheel turning.

astrology.name: Jupiter
astrology.gloss: Jupiter is the planet of expansion and opportunity, widening whatever it touches.

number.gloss: Ten closes one round and opens the next: an ending that is also a reset.

questions: Which season of the wheel are you in, and what does this particular season ask of you?
What stays steady at your centre when your circumstances change?

name: Justice
essence: Clear sight, fair measure, honest consequence.
figure: A laurel-crowned woman in a red robe sits between stone pillars, an upright sword in her right hand and golden scales level in her left, looking steadily out at you. She stands for fairness and accountability: weighing things as they are and owning what follows from a choice.

symbols.meaning: Careful weighing of each side, with nothing added to tip the balance your way.
Clarity that cuts both ways; a decision, once made, has a clean edge.
Willingness to look straight at the facts, including the uncomfortable ones.
A formal frame: this is judgement made openly, with reasons you could state aloud.

upright.short: Look at consequences, fairness and your responsibility in a choice.
upright.meaning: Justice asks for an honest reckoning. It favours looking at what happened, what each person contributed and what a fair response would be. Choices have consequences, and this card treats that as empowering: when you take responsibility for your part, you also recover the ability to change it.
upright.love: Check whether give and take feel fair to both of you, and raise it calmly if they do not.
upright.work: Make the decision on the merits, document your reasoning and apply the same standard to everyone.
upright.self: Own your part in a situation plainly, without excusing yourself or piling on blame.
upright.advice: Before deciding, write down the strongest case for the side you disagree with.

reversed.short: Look for where blame, bias or avoidance is clouding a fair account of events.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the scales are tilted. You may be judging yourself or someone else too harshly, leaving out inconvenient facts, or dodging responsibility for a choice. A sense of unfairness can also linger where a wrong has gone unacknowledged. Balance returns through a fuller, more honest account.
reversed.love: Keeping score, or refusing to acknowledge a hurt, is making it hard for either of you to move on.
reversed.work: A decision feels unfair; ask how it was reached and where your own blind spot might be.
reversed.self: You are either letting yourself off too lightly or sentencing yourself too severely.
reversed.advice: Tell the story of what happened as a neutral witness would, then see what changes.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is reason and language; here it is the clear thinking that separates fact from wish.

astrology.name: Libra
astrology.gloss: Libra is the sign of the scales: balance, fairness and considered agreement.

number.gloss: Eleven stands at the midpoint of the Major Arcana, the hinge on which the scale rests.

questions: What would a fair outcome look like to someone with no stake in your situation?
Which consequence of a past choice are you now ready to take responsibility for?

name: The Hanged Man
essence: A pause that turns the whole view upside down.
figure: A figure hangs by one ankle from the branch of a leafy tree, hands folded behind the head and eyes closed, perfectly at ease, with a sun shining like a halo around their hair and a lakeside town far below. They stand for willing surrender: the insight that comes when you stop struggling and wait.

symbols.meaning: A chosen suspension; the figure could struggle and instead decides to stay with it.
Illumination that arrives in stillness, lighting the mind from an unusual angle.
Hands tucked away from action: nothing to fix, grab or push for the moment.
A pause that is supported and rooted, part of growth and not apart from it.

upright.short: Pause, loosen your grip and try another perspective.
upright.meaning: The Hanged Man favours stopping. When effort has got you nowhere, hanging back and looking at the problem upside down can show you what striving hid. It asks you to give up the need to act for a while, to tolerate not knowing, and to trust that a useful shift in view is forming.
upright.love: Let a question between you stay open a little longer instead of forcing a resolution tonight.
upright.work: A stalled project may need a different angle more than another push; step away and look again.
upright.self: Treat this waiting period as time in which something is quietly rearranging itself.
upright.advice: Ask what you would see if the thing you call a problem were actually the starting point.

reversed.short: Ask whether a pause has become stalling, or struggle is delaying a needed surrender.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the pause has stopped being useful. You might be hanging on in limbo to avoid a decision, giving things up that nobody asked you to give, or thrashing against a delay that would pass more easily if you let it. The card asks which it is: time to come down, or time to stop fighting.
reversed.love: Waiting for the other person to change first has become a way of not choosing for yourself.
reversed.work: Indecision is costing more than either option would; set a point at which you decide.
reversed.self: Putting your own needs on hold indefinitely is not patience, and you are allowed to notice that.
reversed.advice: Decide what you are waiting for, and if you cannot name it, take the next small action.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water yields and reflects; here it is the stillness of floating instead of swimming.

astrology.name: Neptune
astrology.gloss: A modern pairing for dreams and surrender; older tables give this card Water alone.

number.gloss: Twelve completes a full round, like the months of a year, before a new cycle starts.

questions: What might you understand if you stopped trying to solve this for a few days?
Which of your current sacrifices are freely chosen, and which are simply habit?

name: Death
essence: One chapter closes so that another has room to open.
figure: A skeleton rider crowned with white flowers sits a black horse, carrying a black banner marked with a white rose, while lilies bloom at the horse's feet and the sun rests on the horizon beyond. The rider stands for natural endings and the renewal that follows them, as surely as seasons change.

symbols.meaning: New life carried on a dark field: every ending in this card brings a beginning with it.
Change wearing a gentle face; what passes is honoured as well as released.
Light that sets and rises in the same place, marking a threshold between chapters.
Fresh growth already under way in the ground the old chapter leaves behind.

upright.short: An ending makes space for change; release a pattern that has run its course.
upright.meaning: Death is the card of completion. A role, habit, belief or chapter has run its course, and holding on now takes more effort than letting go. It rarely concerns the body; it concerns change that is ready. The card favours a clean, respectful goodbye that leaves space for what comes next.
upright.love: A relationship is changing form; honour what it has been and be honest about what it is now.
upright.work: A project or role has reached its natural end; close it well and note what you are taking with you.
upright.self: An old version of you can be thanked and set down, having done its job.
upright.advice: Choose one thing that is finished and mark its ending with a small, deliberate ritual.

reversed.short: Notice what you keep alive past its season, and what a gentle ending would free.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, an ending is being postponed. You may be keeping something going out of loyalty, habit or uncertainty about what would replace it, and the effort leaves you stuck between chapters. The change can be gradual and kind. It begins with admitting that this season is already over.
reversed.love: You may be staying loyal to how things used to be instead of to how they are today.
reversed.work: Energy is going into propping up something that has stopped giving anything back.
reversed.self: Part of you has already moved on; the remaining part is waiting for permission to follow.
reversed.advice: Finish the sentence 'I am ready to stop' in your own words, then take one modest step toward it.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water transforms what it touches; here it is the deep current that carries things onward.

astrology.name: Scorpio
astrology.gloss: Scorpio is the sign of depth and regeneration, shedding one skin to grow another.

number.gloss: Thirteen follows the complete twelve: the step beyond a finished cycle into a new one.

questions: What in your life has quietly completed itself and is waiting to be let go?
What might have room to grow if you stopped tending something that has finished?

name: Temperance
essence: The right mix, found by patient pouring.
figure: A winged figure with a sun-bright halo stands with one foot in a stream and one on the bank, pouring water in a steady arc from a golden jug into a golden cup, while irises bloom nearby and a rainbow rises over the hills. They stand for moderation, healing and the art of combining opposites.

symbols.meaning: Blending in progress: two different things adjusted, a little at a time, until they suit.

symbols.symbol: One foot in water, one on land
symbols.meaning: Standing in feeling and in practical life at once, with neither abandoned.
Harmony after contrast, many colours held together in a single arc.
Named for a rainbow messenger, they mark this as a place where separate things connect.

upright.short: Blend differences, pace yourself and seek a sustainable middle ground.
upright.meaning: Temperance favours the middle path, found by adjustment instead of by formula. It is the card of mixing: work with rest, your needs with another's, ambition with what your energy can sustain. Progress here is calm and incremental, and it lasts because nothing has been pushed to an extreme.
upright.love: Blend two different temperaments patiently; neither of you has to become the other.
upright.work: Pace the workload so it can be sustained, and combine approaches instead of choosing a single camp.
upright.self: Look for the steady rhythm that leaves you neither wired nor drained by evening.
upright.advice: Adjust one thing by a small amount today, more or less, and observe the difference.

reversed.short: Notice where excess, impatience or all-or-nothing thinking has upset your balance.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the pouring is rushed and the mixture spills. One part of life is taking far more than its share, or you are swinging between extremes with nothing in between. Impatience makes it worse. A return to small, steady measures, and to honest limits, lets things settle into proportion.
reversed.love: One of you is giving or asking for much more than the other; talk about what would feel even.
reversed.work: All-out effort followed by collapse is the pattern; a moderate pace would get further.
reversed.self: You are treating a need as either forbidden or unlimited when a middle amount would serve.
reversed.advice: Pick the area that is most out of proportion and trim or add ten per cent, no more.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire here is tempered heat, the gentle steady flame used to blend and refine.

astrology.name: Sagittarius
astrology.gloss: Sagittarius seeks meaning and the long view, aiming carefully before it lets fly.

number.gloss: Fourteen doubles the seven: a tested resolve brought into balance with its opposite.

questions: Which two parts of your life most need to be brought into better proportion?
What does 'enough' look like for you this week, neither too little nor too much?

name: The Devil
essence: The chain is looser than it looks.
figure: A horned, winged shadow looms against a red sky above two people sitting back to back on stone steps, their wrists joined by a golden chain. The chain hangs slack, and each could slip free. The scene stands for attachment, craving and the habits we keep because we have stopped questioning them.

symbols.meaning: A bond that is loose enough to slip, held in place mostly by habit and belief.
Two people tied together yet unable to see each other: connection without real contact.
The story you tell about having no choice, grown large by never being examined.
Patterns that take hold gradually, one small tendril at a time, until they seem permanent.

upright.short: Notice attachments and habits that limit your freedom to choose.
upright.meaning: The Devil points to whatever has a hold on you: a compulsion, a comfort, a relationship dynamic or a belief that you have no alternative. It is an honest card and a freeing one. Once you see the chain clearly, including what you get from wearing it, you regain the option to take it off.
upright.love: Look at the pull between you honestly: is it mutual choice, or a pattern neither of you has questioned?
upright.work: Golden handcuffs are still handcuffs; ask what keeps you where you are beyond real desire.
upright.self: Bring a habit into the light without shaming yourself; curiosity loosens what judgement tightens.
upright.advice: Name one thing you tell yourself you 'have to' do, and test whether that is actually so.

reversed.short: Loosen one attachment you have already seen clearly, and look at what you were avoiding.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the chain begins to slip. Awareness has arrived, and with it the chance to step away from a pattern that limited you. This can be uncomfortable: without the habit, the feeling it covered comes into view. Stay with that and take small steps, and your room to choose keeps widening.
reversed.love: You are beginning to see a dynamic clearly; changing your own half of it is where freedom starts.
reversed.work: The reasons you felt trapped look thinner under daylight, and other options come into focus.
reversed.self: Self-blame for past habits can become a new chain; let understanding replace self-reproach.
reversed.advice: Remove one small trigger from your day and notice what feeling appears in its place.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is the material world; here it is the pull of comfort, appetite and possession.

astrology.name: Capricorn
astrology.gloss: Capricorn is ambitious and disciplined, and can bind itself tightly to duty and gain.

number.gloss: Fifteen reduces to six, the Lovers' number: choice again, seen from its shadow side.

questions: What do you gain from the habit or attachment you say you want to be free of?
Where are you acting as if you have no choice, and is that really the case?

name: The Tower
essence: What was built on a crack gives way, and the air clears.
figure: A bolt of lightning strikes the crown of a tall stone tower on a crag, scattering blocks and red banners into a stormy sky, while the town beneath stands untouched. Nobody is shown falling. The tower stands for a false structure, a belief, plan or pretence, being cracked open by truth.

symbols.meaning: A flash of clarity that arrives all at once and shows things exactly as they are.

symbols.symbol: The broken crown of the tower
symbols.meaning: The top of a rigid structure opening up; a certainty that could not hold.
Old allegiances and labels coming loose, no longer flying over you.
The ground itself is intact, ready to carry something built more honestly.

upright.short: Question an unstable assumption and rebuild on something honest.
upright.meaning: The Tower describes a sudden shift in how things stand. Something built on a shaky assumption can no longer hold, and its cracking brings both a jolt and relief. The card favours honesty over repair work. Let what was unsound come down, look at the bare ground, and rebuild on what is true.
upright.love: A hard truth has surfaced or needs to; honesty may shake things, and it also clears the air.
upright.work: A plan or structure is proving unsound; treat it as information and redesign from the facts.
upright.self: A story you told about yourself is breaking open, making room for a more accurate one.
upright.advice: Ask what this shake-up has revealed that you could not see before, and write it down.

reversed.short: Notice a change you are bracing against, and what clinging to the old structure costs.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the shake-up is happening slowly or on the inside. You may sense that something cannot continue and be working hard to keep it standing, or be picking through the aftermath of a change that has already happened. Either way, gentleness helps: dismantle by choice what will not hold.
reversed.love: Avoiding a necessary conversation keeps the walls up and the tension inside them.
reversed.work: You can see the cracks; raising them now is easier than patching them again.
reversed.self: An inner change is under way that others cannot yet see; give it time and plain language.
reversed.advice: Choose one thing you know is unsound and take the first step to change it yourself.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire here is the sudden spark, the flash that clears away what was hollow.

astrology.name: Mars
astrology.gloss: Mars is the planet of force and action, breaking a deadlock so movement can resume.

number.gloss: Sixteen reduces to seven, the Chariot's number: direction regained after a hard stop.

questions: Which assumption in your life has been showing cracks that you keep painting over?
If you could rebuild one part of your life on honest ground, where would you begin?

name: The Star
essence: Calm after the storm, and water for dry ground.
figure: A woman in a star-patterned robe kneels at the edge of a moonlit pool, pouring water from two golden jugs, one into the pool and one onto the bank, while one great star and seven smaller ones shine overhead. She stands for hope, renewal and trust quietly restored.

symbols.meaning: Giving back to the source and to the land at once: replenishing both feeling and daily life.
A fixed point to steer by, far off and reliable, when nearer lights have gone out.
Many small sources of light; hope rarely depends on a single thing.
Calm water set gently in motion, a sign that recovery has begun.

upright.short: Make space for renewal, hope and small acts of restoration.
upright.meaning: The Star follows difficulty with a long, clear breath. It favours gentle restoration: small, regular acts that refill what has been emptied, and faith that things can improve without being forced. Nothing here is dramatic. It is the quiet return of trust in yourself and in the future.
upright.love: Openness returns slowly; offer and accept small kindnesses without rushing to define things.
upright.work: Reconnect with why this work mattered to you; let that purpose guide the next modest step.
upright.self: You are mending, even if unevenly; notice the small signs that your energy is returning.
upright.advice: Do one small restorative thing today and let it count, however minor it seems.

reversed.short: Tend a hope that has dimmed; restoration can begin smaller than you expect.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the stars are still there and clouds are in the way. Discouragement may have convinced you that effort is pointless, or you may be so busy pouring out for others that nothing flows back to you. Hope here is a practice more than a feeling: begin with one small act of care.
reversed.love: Guardedness after a hurt is understandable; it may also be blocking the comfort that is on offer.
reversed.work: Cynicism about the job is hiding a wish for it to mean something; name that wish.
reversed.self: You have stopped doing the small things that restore you because they seemed too slight to matter.
reversed.advice: Pick up one abandoned habit that used to help, and do the easiest possible version of it.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is clear thought and wide horizons; here it is the open night sky after rain.

astrology.name: Aquarius
astrology.gloss: Aquarius is the water-bearer: hopeful, humane and looking toward what could be.

number.gloss: Seventeen reduces to eight, Strength's number: resilience renewed gently and often.

questions: What small act reliably restores you, and when did you last allow yourself to do it?
What do you still hope for when you set aside what seems realistic?

name: The Moon
essence: A winding path, walked by lantern light.
figure: A cloaked walker carrying a lantern pauses on a winding path beneath an enormous crescent moon, with a dog on one side and a howling wolf on the other, two towers in the distance and a lake glimmering between them. The scene stands for uncertainty, imagination and the half-lit realm of instinct.

symbols.meaning: The tame and the wild sides of instinct, both responding to the same pull.
Partial light: enough to move by, too little to be certain of what you are seeing.
A way forward that cannot be seen whole, only walked one bend at a time.
Your own small, steady attention, more use in the dark than any amount of guessing.
A gateway into unfamiliar ground; beyond them the map has not been drawn.

upright.short: Uncertainty calls for curiosity; separate fear from evidence.
upright.meaning: The Moon describes a time when things are unclear and feelings run high. Shapes in the half-light can look like threats or wonders, and it is hard to tell which. The card favours curiosity and patience: move slowly, check your impressions, and let instinct and evidence inform each other.
upright.love: Assumptions thrive in ambiguity; ask what the other person means instead of filling in the gap.
upright.work: You do not have the full picture yet; proceed in small steps and verify as you go.
upright.self: Dreams, moods and odd hunches carry information now; note them without taking them as fact.
upright.advice: List what you actually know on one side and what you are imagining on the other.

reversed.short: Let confusion settle: check which worry has evidence and which is only shadow.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the mist either starts to lift or thickens because you have been avoiding a look at it. Misunderstandings come to light, and anxieties you kept to yourself turn out smaller when spoken. If you have been telling yourself a comforting story, this is a gentle prompt to compare it with the facts.
reversed.love: A misunderstanding is ready to be cleared up; say what you assumed and ask what was meant.
reversed.work: Something left vague is causing confusion downstream; get it in plain words.
reversed.self: A worry kept private has grown in the dark; sharing it with one person shrinks it to size.
reversed.advice: Say one unspoken worry out loud to someone steady and notice how it sounds in daylight.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is the tide of feeling; here it is deep, moonlit and hard to see the bottom of.

astrology.name: Pisces
astrology.gloss: Pisces is dreamy and porous, at home in imagination and in what cannot be pinned down.

number.gloss: Eighteen reduces to nine, the Hermit's number: finding your way by a single small light.

questions: What are you sure of, and what are you only guessing at in the half-light?
Which of your instincts has proved trustworthy before, and what is it telling you now?

name: The Sun
essence: Daylight, warmth and nothing to hide.
figure: A laughing rider in yellow, red scarf flying, flings both arms wide on the back of a white horse as it wades through a field of sunflowers beneath an enormous sun. The reins are forgotten. The rider stands for uncomplicated joy, vitality and the confidence of being seen as you are.

symbols.meaning: Full light with no shadow to squint through: clarity, warmth and plain visibility.
Openness with nothing guarded, a body that trusts the moment enough to let go.
Simple, honest energy carrying you along without needing to be driven.
Growth that turns toward what feeds it, and thrives by doing so.

upright.short: Welcome clarity, playfulness and the simple pleasure of being present.
upright.meaning: The Sun is the card of things going well in the open. It favours play, straightforwardness and letting yourself enjoy what is good without waiting for a catch. Confusion gives way to clear sight, and energy is high. The only request is that you actually turn up for it, fully present.
upright.love: Enjoy each other simply: laughter, daylight and affection with no agenda attached.
upright.work: Your efforts are visible and well received; share the credit and let yourself be pleased.
upright.self: Do something for the pure fun of it and let that be a good enough reason.
upright.advice: Step outside, literally if you can, and give ten minutes to something that delights you.

reversed.short: Find the joy that is dimmed or postponed, and let a small pleasure count.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the light is still there and something is shading it. You may be too tired or too busy to enjoy what is going well, or putting on brightness you do not feel. Sometimes it marks confidence that has outrun the facts. Honest rest, and one small unforced pleasure, let the warmth back in.
reversed.love: You are both going through the motions of fun; ask what would feel playful to each of you now.
reversed.work: Success feels flat because you are worn out; recovery belongs on the plan.
reversed.self: You keep postponing enjoyment until everything is finished, and everything is never finished.
reversed.advice: Allow yourself one small pleasure today without earning it or explaining it.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is life-force and warmth; here it shines at full, generous strength.

astrology.name: Sun
astrology.gloss: The Sun is the centre of the chart: identity, vitality and the self you show the world.

number.gloss: Nineteen reduces to ten and then to one: a cycle completed and a bright new start.

questions: What brings you uncomplicated joy, and how much room does it have in your week?
Where could you afford to be more open and less guarded than you are?

name: Judgement
essence: A clear call, and the choice to answer it.
figure: A winged herald sounds a long golden trumpet through a break in the clouds, and below a small crowd of every age looks up into the light, one with a hand pressed to the heart. They stand for awakening: the moment you hear what your life is asking and rise to meet it.

symbols.meaning: A summons you cannot unhear, clear enough to cut through routine and distraction.
People of different ages responding together: it is never too early or too late to answer.
Recognition felt in the body first, a sense that this message is meant for you.
A sudden opening in what seemed fixed, letting a wider view pour through.

upright.short: Reflect honestly and answer a call to grow beyond an old story.
upright.meaning: Judgement is a card of honest review followed by a fresh start. It favours looking back over what you have done, forgiving what can be forgiven, and deciding who you intend to be from here. A call is sounding: toward a change, a purpose or a truer version of yourself. The card asks you to respond.
upright.love: Clear the air about the past so that you can meet each other as you are today.
upright.work: A vocation or a change of direction is making itself heard; take the signal seriously.
upright.self: Review your recent chapter with honesty and mercy in equal measure, then choose again.
upright.advice: Write down what you feel called toward and one thing you would need to release to answer.

reversed.short: Hear the call you keep postponing, and ease the self-criticism that drowns it out.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the trumpet is sounding and you have your hands over your ears. Harsh self-judgement, old regret or doubt about whether you deserve a new start keeps you where you are. The card suggests that the verdict you dread exists mainly in your own head. Mercy toward yourself lets you hear clearly.
reversed.love: Holding an old mistake over yourself or a partner keeps you both living in the past.
reversed.work: You know which change you want and keep finding reasons why now is the wrong moment.
reversed.self: Your inner judge is far harsher than any fair one would be; question its evidence.
reversed.advice: Forgive yourself for one specific thing, in writing, and note what that makes possible.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire here is the wake-up spark, a light that rouses what had gone dormant.

astrology.name: Pluto
astrology.gloss: A modern pairing for deep renewal; older tables give Judgement the element of Fire alone.

number.gloss: Twenty reduces to two, the High Priestess's number: inner knowing finally spoken aloud.

questions: What have you been hearing a call toward that you keep explaining away?
What would you need to forgive, in yourself or another, to begin again cleanly?

name: The World
essence: The circle closes, and you are whole inside it.
figure: A dancer in white moves freely inside a great wreath of leaves and white flowers, a long red ribbon swirling around her, while winged lions, an eagle and a white bull look on from the four corners. She stands for completion and integration: a journey finished and fully lived.

symbols.meaning: A finished circle, a boundary that marks something as complete and worth celebrating.
Ease and freedom inside limits; mastery that has become graceful.
The thread of experience, every twist of the journey gathered into one flowing line.
Lions, an eagle and a bull: steady witnesses framing an achievement, as they once framed change.

upright.short: Recognise a completed cycle and carry its lessons into what follows.
upright.meaning: The World marks a cycle brought to a satisfying close. Something you have worked on, lived through or grown into has come together, and you can see how the pieces fit. It favours pausing to recognise that fully before starting anew, so that what you learned travels with you.
upright.love: A relationship reaches a settled, mature stage; celebrate how far you have come together.
upright.work: A long piece of work is complete or nearly so; finish properly and take in the achievement.
upright.self: You are more integrated than you used to be; the scattered parts have learned to move together.
upright.advice: Mark a recent completion in some visible way before you look at what comes next.

reversed.short: Name what remains unfinished, and take the last step that would let a cycle close.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the circle is nearly drawn and has not quite closed. A final step is being put off, loose ends are trailing, or you have rushed on without acknowledging what was achieved. Fulfilment feels oddly out of reach. The remedy is specific: find the unfinished piece and complete it.
reversed.love: Something from an earlier chapter is unresolved and keeps asking for a proper conclusion.
reversed.work: The last five per cent is being avoided; decide what 'done' means and reach it.
reversed.self: You have moved the goalposts on yourself again; notice what you have already accomplished.
reversed.advice: List the loose ends on one thing and tie off the smallest of them today.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is the tangible result; here it is the finished, solid form of a long effort.

astrology.name: Saturn
astrology.gloss: Saturn is the planet of time, limits and maturity, rewarding what is built patiently.

number.gloss: Twenty-one is the final numbered step: three sevens, a whole journey seen through.

questions: What have you completed recently that you have not yet stopped to acknowledge?
Which unfinished thing, once closed, would let you feel free to start something new?

name: Ace of Wands
essence: A live spark, offered to whoever will pick it up.
figure: A hand reaches out of a bank of cloud gripping a rough branch that has burst into green leaf, with a sunburst blazing behind it and stray leaves drifting down. No person is shown, only the offer. It stands for raw creative energy: the first flare of an idea that wants to be acted on.

symbols.meaning: Dead-looking wood putting out leaves: energy returning, and an idea that is alive.
Inspiration arriving unasked, held out for you to take or to leave.
Enthusiasm at full brightness, lighting everything around the new idea.
Sparks scatter quickly; a new impulse needs catching before it drifts away.

upright.short: A creative spark asks for a small first experiment; enthusiasm needs an outlet.
upright.meaning: The Ace of Wands is the urge to begin. An idea, a desire or a burst of energy has turned up, and it carries more heat than detail. The card favours a quick, small trial over a long plan: light the match, see whether it catches, and let the doing teach you what the idea really is.
upright.love: A fresh spark of attraction or renewed interest wants expression; say the warm thing aloud.
upright.work: Pitch the idea while it excites you, or build the roughest possible version this week.
upright.self: Follow what gives you energy and treat that liveliness as a clue worth trusting.
upright.advice: Give your newest idea twenty minutes of real attention before the day ends.

reversed.short: A spark is flickering; find what is dampening it before forcing a start.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the branch is in your hand and the spark is slow to catch. Motivation dips, a promising beginning fizzles, or you have so many ideas that none gets lit. Nothing is wrong with you. The fuel may simply be damp: rest, a clearer reason or a smaller first step can change that.
reversed.love: Interest is present and going unexpressed; ask yourself what makes showing it feel risky.
reversed.work: You keep preparing to start; lower the bar until beginning becomes almost effortless.
reversed.self: Flat energy is a message about what you need, and need not be read as a character flaw.
reversed.advice: Ask what would make this feel exciting again, and change that one condition.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is drive, appetite and creativity; this card is its very first flame.

astrology.name: Fire signs
astrology.gloss: Aces hold their whole element in seed form: Aries, Leo and Sagittarius together.

number.gloss: One is the seed: all the potential of the suit packed into a single starting point.

questions: What idea has been warming in the back of your mind, waiting for a first experiment?
What gives you energy at the moment, and how could you follow it a little further?

name: Two of Wands
essence: The world in your hand, and a decision about how far to go.
figure: A red-cloaked traveller with a pack on their back stands between two tall staffs on a hilltop and holds a small globe, looking out over a harbour town of domes, red roofs and sails. They stand for the planner at a threshold: someone who has achieved something and is weighing a bigger move.

symbols.meaning: The wider world held small enough to study; possibilities being measured before the journey.
What you have already built stands at one hand, and what you might reach for at the other.
A safe, familiar base, comfortable enough to make leaving it a real choice.
Readiness to go; the preparations are made and only the decision remains.

upright.short: Look beyond the familiar and make a plan before expanding your ambitions.
upright.meaning: The Two of Wands is the pause between an early success and the next, larger step. You can see further from here than you could before, and the question is what to do with that view. It favours mapping the route, weighing known comfort against wider possibility, and choosing deliberately.
upright.love: Talk about where you would each like life to go, including the places you have not been yet.
upright.work: Draft the longer-range plan: where this could lead in a year, and what the first leg requires.
upright.self: Let yourself want something bigger than your present circumstances without apologising for it.
upright.advice: Sketch two possible futures on paper and note which one you keep returning to.

reversed.short: Notice where fear of the unfamiliar keeps a wider plan safely on paper.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the globe stays in your hand and the pack stays on the ground. Planning has become a place to hide, or the familiar harbour feels too comfortable to leave. You might also be thinking too small. The card nudges you to test one option in the real world instead of perfecting the map.
reversed.love: You are keeping a relationship in a safe, known shape because growth feels unpredictable.
reversed.work: The plan has been revised many times and launched none; pick a date for a first move.
reversed.self: Ask whether you are choosing comfort, or whether comfort is choosing for you.
reversed.advice: Turn one item from your long-term plan into something you can try in the coming days.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is ambition; here it is banked and thoughtful, looking before it leaps.

astrology.name: Mars in Aries
astrology.gloss: Bold energy in the pioneer's sign: the will to claim new ground and lead the way.

number.gloss: Two is a choice between paths, the moment of balance before commitment.

questions: If you knew you would be fine either way, which larger plan would you start on?
What does your comfortable harbour give you, and what does it keep you from?

name: Three of Wands
essence: Ships launched, eyes on the horizon.
figure: A woman in a long red cloak stands with her back to us and one hand on her hip, three staffs planted beside her, watching sailing ships cross a wide blue bay toward distant mountains. She stands for the venture already under way: effort sent out into the world and the confidence to wait for its return.

symbols.meaning: Plans already launched, carrying your work outward beyond where you can steer it.
A firm base camp; what has been established supports what is being attempted.
Relaxed confidence, the posture of someone who trusts the groundwork they laid.
The longer goal, still distant, giving the present effort its direction.

upright.short: An effort is taking shape; consider the wider horizon and what comes next.
upright.meaning: The Three of Wands shows early results appearing. Something you set in motion is moving, and you can afford to lift your eyes to what follows. It favours thinking bigger, looking further ahead and preparing to receive what returns. Patience matters here too: ships take time to cross water.
upright.love: A connection is developing nicely; look ahead together and speak of shared plans.
upright.work: First results are coming in; use them to plan the next stage and widen your reach.
upright.self: Acknowledge that your earlier effort is paying off, and let that build your confidence.
upright.advice: Review what you have already launched and choose the next horizon to aim for.

reversed.short: Check what delays are teaching you, and whether your plans reach far enough.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the ships are slow to return or were never sent far enough. Delays test your patience, results fall short of the forecast, or the plan stops at the harbour mouth. It is a prompt to review: is this a matter of waiting, of adjusting course, or of daring a longer voyage?
reversed.love: You are leaving all the planning to the other person; offer one idea of your own.
reversed.work: A delay is frustrating you; use the gap to strengthen the part of the plan that was thin.
reversed.self: Impatience with slow progress is hiding how much has already been set in motion.
reversed.advice: Pick one stalled effort and decide: wait, adjust or relaunch it with a clearer aim.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is enterprise; here it reaches outward, warming things at a distance.

astrology.name: Sun in Aries
astrology.gloss: Confidence and vitality in the sign of beginnings: a young venture in full light.

number.gloss: Three is first fruit: an initial result that shows the effort can grow.

questions: Which of your efforts is already at sea, and what would help you trust its progress?
How far ahead are you looking, and what lies just beyond that horizon?

name: Four of Wands
essence: A doorway of flowers, and friends beneath it.
figure: Four tall posts are joined by a garland of leaves, white flowers and red ribbons, and beneath it a knot of friends laugh together, two of them lifting golden goblets, with a sunlit hill town behind. They stand for celebration, homecoming and the people who make a place feel like yours.

symbols.meaning: A simple structure made festive: stability dressed up for a happy occasion.
A toast to something achieved together, marked out loud so that it registers.
Belonging: joy that multiplies because it is shared.
Home ground, the community that stands behind the celebration.

upright.short: Celebrate a shared milestone and the people who make a place feel welcoming.
upright.meaning: The Four of Wands is a card of glad arrival. A stage has been completed, a foundation holds, and it is time to stop and enjoy it with others. It favours gatherings, welcomes and marking milestones properly. The stability here is warm and open-sided: a canopy people can walk in under.
upright.love: Celebrate where you have got to together, and let friends and family share in it.
upright.work: Mark the milestone with the team; recognition now strengthens the next phase.
upright.self: Notice where you feel at home and with whom, and spend time there on purpose.
upright.advice: Invite someone to celebrate a recent win with you, however modest it seems.

reversed.short: Ask what would make home or community feel settled, and name the unmarked milestone.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the garland hangs unevenly. Home may be in flux, a group may feel less welcoming than it used to, or a real achievement has passed without anyone raising a glass. The joy is quieter or more private at present. Tending your sense of belonging, even in small ways, steadies the posts.
reversed.love: Different ideas about home or commitment are surfacing; talk about what settled means to each of you.
reversed.work: The team is between phases and morale is patchy; acknowledge the wins that were skipped over.
reversed.self: You have not paused to recognise how far you have come; a private celebration still counts.
reversed.advice: Do one small thing that makes your space, or your circle, feel more like home.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is the hearth here: warmth that gathers people around it.

astrology.name: Venus in Aries
astrology.gloss: Affection and pleasure meeting bold energy: the joy of celebrating a fresh success.

number.gloss: Four is a firm foundation, four corners that let you rest and invite others in.

questions: Who would you want standing beside you under the garland, and have you told them?
What milestone have you passed lately without stopping to mark it?

name: Five of Wands
essence: Five voices, five staffs, one crowded hillside.
figure: Five young people scramble on a grassy slope, each swinging a staff, the sticks crossing in mid-air at every angle while nobody quite lands a blow. It looks more like rough sparring than a real fight. They stand for competition, clashing opinions and the friction of many wills in one place.

symbols.meaning: Ideas and wills colliding; energy spent against one another instead of in one direction.
Everyone for themselves, each convinced their own angle is the right one.
A contest more than a battle: friction that can sharpen as easily as it can wear down.
Plenty of room for everyone, if the scramble could turn into a formation.

upright.short: Competing ideas create friction; distinguish useful challenge from needless rivalry.
upright.meaning: The Five of Wands describes lively conflict. People want different things, or the same thing, and the result is noise, jostling and a great deal of energy. It is not necessarily hostile. The card asks you to tell the useful kind of challenge, which improves ideas, from squabbling that only tires everyone.
upright.love: Bickering may be a clumsy bid for attention; find out what each of you is really asking for.
upright.work: Competing agendas are slowing the group; agree the goal first, then argue about methods.
upright.self: Several of your own wants are shouting at once; let each have its say in turn.
upright.advice: In your next disagreement, state the other person's point fairly before making yours.

reversed.short: Notice a conflict you are avoiding or prolonging, and what would actually settle it.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the sparring either winds down or goes underground. You may be sidestepping a disagreement to keep the peace, leaving the tension unspoken, or feeling worn out by a quarrel that has run too long. Common ground exists. Reaching it means saying openly what the scuffle was about.
reversed.love: Keeping quiet to avoid an argument is storing it up; raise the small thing kindly now.
reversed.work: The rivalry has become draining; propose terms for working together or step out of the contest.
reversed.self: An inner argument eases when you stop needing one side to win outright.
reversed.advice: Ask one person you have been at odds with what a fair settlement would look like to them.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is competitive heat here: sparks thrown when strong wills rub together.

astrology.name: Saturn in Leo
astrology.gloss: Limits pressing on pride: each ego tested against the others, and tempered by it.

number.gloss: Five disrupts the stable four; it brings challenge, change and the need to adapt.

questions: Which of your current conflicts sharpens you, and which simply wears you out?
What are you actually competing for, and is it worth the energy you spend?

name: Six of Wands
essence: Riding home with the wreath, and the crowd that helped.
figure: A rider in gilded armour and a laurel crown sits a white horse, holding up a staff topped with a wreath and red ribbon, while five companions on foot raise their own staffs in salute along a hillside path. The rider stands for public success: achievement seen, named and cheered.

symbols.meaning: Recognition made visible, a sign that others have noticed what you accomplished.
Being lifted into view; success raises you where everyone can see.
Supporters whose effort is part of the win, keeping pace beside the rider.
A moment of acclaim, lovely and brief, to be enjoyed while it is in the air.

upright.short: Accept recognition for progress while remembering the people who helped you get here.
upright.meaning: The Six of Wands is the card of deserved recognition. Work has paid off and people are noticing. It favours accepting praise gracefully, letting yourself be seen and sharing the moment with those who walked beside you. Confidence gained here is fuel, so long as the wreath does not become the goal.
upright.love: Tell your partner what you admire in them, and allow their pride in you to land.
upright.work: Your contribution is being acknowledged; accept it and name the colleagues who made it possible.
upright.self: Let a compliment stay with you for a moment instead of batting it away.
upright.advice: Say thank you, without a disclaimer, the next time someone praises your work.

reversed.short: Ask whose approval you are chasing, and recognise your own progress first.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the parade is quiet. Effort may have gone unnoticed, or you may be measuring your worth by applause and feeling its absence keenly. Sometimes the card points the other way, to pride that forgets the people on foot. The steadier path is to know for yourself what you did well.
reversed.love: Wanting to be admired more than known can keep real closeness at arm's length.
reversed.work: Credit has gone elsewhere or nowhere; state your contribution factually and without heat.
reversed.self: You are waiting for someone else to say you did well before you believe it.
reversed.advice: Write down three things you handled well recently and read them back as if about a friend.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is glowing confidence here, a flame held up where others can see it.

astrology.name: Jupiter in Leo
astrology.gloss: Generous, expansive luck in the sign of the spotlight: success that enjoys an audience.

number.gloss: Six restores harmony after struggle: effort and reward come back into balance.

questions: Whose recognition matters most to you, and why that person in particular?
Who helped you reach a recent success, and do they know you noticed?

name: Seven of Wands
essence: High ground, held with one staff against six.
figure: A bearded figure in a red cape stands braced on a rocky outcrop, gripping a staff across the body, while six more staffs thrust up from unseen hands below. The stance is firm, even with the odds stacked. This is the defender: someone holding a position they believe in under pressure.

symbols.meaning: An advantage already earned; you are defending ground you have every right to stand on.
Challenges arriving from several directions at once, faceless and persistent.
Feet set wide: resolve expressed through the whole body, without any need to strike.
