One clear conviction, enough to hold the line when it is gripped with both hands.

upright.short: Hold a meaningful boundary when challenged; choose what is worth defending.
upright.meaning: The Seven of Wands shows you holding your position while others push against it. Success or a clear stance has drawn challenge, and the card favours standing firm on what truly matters. It also asks you to choose your hill: some ground deserves defending, and some can be given up without loss.
upright.love: State a boundary calmly and keep to it; the right people adjust to a clear line.
upright.work: Defend your idea with evidence and composure, and concede the points that are fair.
upright.self: Trust a conviction you reached carefully, even if it is unpopular in the room.
upright.advice: Decide which one thing you are not willing to give way on, and say it without apology.

reversed.short: Check if you are defending out of habit, or yielding ground that truly matters.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the footing slips. You may be worn down by constant pushback and tempted to give up ground you care about, or so used to defending that you treat every question as an attack. The card asks for a sorting: what deserves your energy, and where could you simply lower the staff?
reversed.love: Defensiveness is turning ordinary feedback into a fight; listen once before you answer.
reversed.work: You are battling on too many fronts; drop the ones that do not serve the main aim.
reversed.self: Being on guard all the time is exhausting you, and not every challenge is a threat.
reversed.advice: Let one minor point go today, and save your strength for the one that counts.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is courage under pressure here: heat that holds its place instead of spreading.

astrology.name: Mars in Leo
astrology.gloss: Fighting spirit joined to pride: fierce defence of what you have made your own.

number.gloss: Seven is a test of commitment; what you believe is pushed to see whether it holds.

questions: Which hill in your life is truly worth holding, and which are you defending from habit?
What would change if you assumed the challenge in front of you was a question, not an attack?

name: Eight of Wands
essence: Everything in the air at once, and landing fast.
figure: Eight wands streak in a diagonal flight across a bright sky, trailing fire and scraps of leaf, high above a river valley and a small town. Nobody appears in the picture: only movement. The image stands for speed, news and events gathering pace once the obstacles have cleared.

symbols.meaning: Many things moving together in a shared direction, close to arriving.
Energy released; delay has ended and momentum has taken over.
A clear path with nothing in the way, so that speed becomes possible.
The place where all this is about to land, calm for the moment.

upright.short: Momentum and messages gather speed; coordinate your response before rushing ahead.
upright.meaning: The Eight of Wands is quick. Messages arrive, plans accelerate and things that were stuck begin to move all at once. It favours responsiveness: answer, decide, travel, send. The one caution is aim. Fast-moving things land where they are pointed, so spend a moment checking the direction.
upright.love: Communication flows easily; send the message, make the call, close the distance.
upright.work: Things are speeding up; clear your desk, reply promptly and keep the priorities in order.
upright.self: Enjoy the feeling of flow, and keep enough structure that you can steer inside it.
upright.advice: Deal with the three messages you have been sitting on before anything else today.

reversed.short: Momentum is scattered or stalled; sort the signals before you answer in haste.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the wands wobble in flight. Messages cross, timings slip or a rush of activity sends effort in conflicting directions. You may be hurrying a reply that needs thought, or waiting impatiently on news. Slowing by a single beat and confirming the facts usually untangles things.
reversed.love: A hasty text or a long silence is being misread; check the meaning before reacting.
reversed.work: Too many things launched at once are colliding; sequence them and confirm who has which.
reversed.self: Restlessness is pushing you to act simply to end the waiting; breathe before you send.
reversed.advice: Before replying in a hurry, read the message twice and answer the question that was asked.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is swift here: a flash that travels quickly from one place to the next.

astrology.name: Mercury in Sagittarius
astrology.gloss: The messenger in the archer's sign: quick words and long-distance aim.

number.gloss: Eight is movement and rhythm, energy repeating itself until it gathers real pace.

questions: What has started moving quickly in your life, and where is it pointed?
Which reply or decision have you been delaying that would free things up?

name: Nine of Wands
essence: Tired, bandaged and still at the wall.
figure: A bandaged guard, red cloak around the shoulders, rests on a low stone wall, both hands wrapped around one staff, glancing warily to the side, with eight more staffs standing behind like a fence. They stand for resilience late in a long effort: wary, weary and unwilling to give up so close to the end.

symbols.meaning: Past knocks that taught something; experience worn openly instead of hidden.
Defences built from earlier efforts, protective and also a little confining.
Vigilance that has become a reflex, watching for trouble that may not be coming.
A rest taken without leaving the post, strength being gathered for a final stretch.

upright.short: Past effort has made you cautious; protect your energy without shutting everything out.
upright.meaning: The Nine of Wands is about staying power. You have been through a great deal with this, and it shows, yet you remain standing. The card favours one more round of effort, taken wisely: guard your reserves, use what the earlier knocks taught you, and keep enough openness to accept help.
upright.love: Old hurts make you careful; let caution inform you without letting it decide everything.
upright.work: You are close to the finish and tired; pace the final push and protect your recovery time.
upright.self: Give yourself credit for how much you have already come through to reach this point.
upright.advice: Rest properly once before the last effort, and ask one person to share the watch.

reversed.short: Notice where guardedness has hardened into walls, or exhaustion needs real rest.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the guard is running on empty. Tiredness is close to burnout, or wariness has grown until everyone looks like a threat and nobody is allowed near. You may be tempted to walk off just before the end. Real rest, and lowering the fence for someone trustworthy, restores more than gritting on.
reversed.love: Expecting to be hurt, you keep a partner outside the wall and then feel alone inside it.
reversed.work: You cannot finish this on fumes; negotiate a pause or a hand before your judgement suffers.
reversed.self: Constant bracing has become your normal, and your body is asking to stand down.
reversed.advice: Take one item off your watch list and hand it, fully, to someone else.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is the banked ember here: low, guarded and still alight after a long night.

astrology.name: Moon in Sagittarius
astrology.gloss: Restless feeling in a far-seeking sign: instinct kept on watch through a long journey.

number.gloss: Nine is the threshold before completion, where endurance is tested one last time.

questions: What have your past setbacks taught you that is truly useful now?
Where is your guard still needed, and where has it outlived the danger?

name: Ten of Wands
essence: Carrying it all, and unable to see the road.
figure: A walker seen from behind bends almost double under a roped bundle of ten heavy staffs, trudging up a stony track toward a hill town with a tall tower. The load hides their view of the way ahead. They stand for overcommitment: responsibility taken on until the purpose behind it is lost from sight.

symbols.meaning: Every task and duty gathered into one load, more than a single back was built for.
Effort without ease, the body showing a cost the mind keeps overriding.
With head down under the weight, it is hard to see where you are going or why.
The destination is close and real; the open question is how much needs carrying there.

upright.short: Too much responsibility obscures the goal; share a burden or put one task down.
upright.meaning: The Ten of Wands shows the weight of having said yes to everything. Success has brought obligations, and you are hauling them all yourself. The card respects your effort and questions its shape. It favours stopping to ask which sticks are truly yours, which can be shared and which could be set down.
upright.love: Carrying the whole emotional load alone breeds quiet resentment; ask for a fairer split.
upright.work: You have taken on too much; delegate, renegotiate a deadline or drop the least important task.
upright.self: Being reliable has turned into being overloaded; your worth is not measured in weight carried.
upright.advice: List everything you are carrying and cross off, hand over or postpone one item today.

reversed.short: Notice which load you are ready to put down, and which was never yours to carry.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the bundle is slipping, by choice or by exhaustion. You may finally be putting things down, handing some over and feeling the relief of a lighter step. Or you may be gripping harder as the load threatens to scatter. The kinder route is to release some of it before your back decides for you.
reversed.love: You can stop managing everything for both of you; let your partner carry their own share.
reversed.work: Something has to give; choosing what to drop is better than waiting to see what falls.
reversed.self: Notice the belief that nobody else could do it properly, and test it once.
reversed.advice: Hand over one responsibility completely, without checking afterwards how it was done.

element.name: Fire
element.gloss: Fire is overextended here: so many flames to tend that none of them can warm you.

astrology.name: Saturn in Sagittarius
astrology.gloss: Duty weighing on a free spirit: big aims that have become a heavy obligation.

number.gloss: Ten is the suit at its fullest, so complete that it tips over into excess.

questions: Which of the things you carry would you put down first if you were allowed to?
What were you working toward before the load grew so heavy that it blocked the view?

name: Page of Wands
essence: A curious beginner, turning a new idea over in the light.
figure: A young traveller in a red scarf sits cross-legged on dry desert ground, a satchel at their side, holding up a short wand tipped with fresh leaves and studying it closely. Bare mesas stretch behind. They stand for the enthusiastic beginner: full of ideas, eager to explore and not yet sure where it leads.

symbols.meaning: A new interest showing its first leaves, examined with fascination before being put to use.
Open, unclaimed ground where a spark has room to become whatever it likes.
Travelling light and ready to move; this is someone at the start of a journey.
A flash of boldness worn loosely, courage that is still playful.

upright.short: Explore a bold idea with beginner's curiosity before deciding where it will lead.
upright.meaning: The Page of Wands brings the energy of a new enthusiasm. Something has caught your interest and you want to find out more. The card favours exploring without pressure to be good at it yet: ask questions, try things, follow the thread. Its gift is the freedom of not having decided anything.
upright.love: Flirt with possibility; be openly curious about someone without scripting the outcome.
upright.work: Volunteer for the unfamiliar task and learn as you go; beginner's energy is an asset here.
upright.self: Let yourself be a keen amateur at something purely because it interests you.
upright.advice: Spend an hour exploring a new interest with no goal beyond finding out what it is like.

reversed.short: An idea is restless or unformed; give your enthusiasm one place to land.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, enthusiasm scatters before it roots. You may be hopping between interests, talking up plans that never begin, or losing heart the moment novelty fades. The spark is real and needs a little shelter. Choosing one idea and giving it a simple first task turns restlessness into a start.
reversed.love: Excitement cools quickly once things become real; ask what you are actually looking for.
reversed.work: Many starts and few follow-throughs; finish a small piece to prove the idea to yourself.
reversed.self: Boredom may be a sign that you need a challenge, not a sign that nothing is worth doing.
reversed.advice: Pick the idea you mention most often and take one concrete step on it today.

element.name: Earth of Fire
element.gloss: The Page gives fire somewhere to stand: a spark set down on solid ground to see if it takes.

astrology.name: Fire signs
astrology.gloss: No one sign belongs to this Page, who apprentices to Aries, Leo and Sagittarius alike.

number.name: Page
number.gloss: The Page is the student of the suit, learning its energy with fresh and open eyes.

questions: What have you become curious about lately that you have not yet let yourself explore?
When did you last try something purely for the fun of being a beginner?

name: Knight of Wands
essence: All fire and forward motion, hooves off the ground.
figure: A rider in armour and a streaming red cape urges a bay horse into a leap, auburn hair flying and a leafy wand held high like a torch, with dust billowing beneath. Everything in the picture surges forward. The rider stands for passion in action: adventure, daring and a hunger to get going.

symbols.meaning: Momentum that has already left the ground; commitment made with the whole body.
Purpose carried like a torch, visible to everyone and leading from the front.
Speed made visible, with a hint of showmanship in how the charge is made.
What gets kicked up behind bold action, for someone else to see through.

upright.short: Move with adventurous energy, giving your excitement enough direction to last.
upright.meaning: The Knight of Wands charges. This card favours bold moves, travel, and throwing yourself into what excites you. Its energy is magnetic and gets things started that caution never would. To make it last, give the fire a destination and a pace the horse can keep up beyond the first mile.
upright.love: Pursue with warmth and honesty, and check that your enthusiasm leaves room for theirs.
upright.work: Take the initiative on the ambitious project, and line up the follow-through as you launch.
upright.self: Say yes to the adventure that scares you a little in an exciting way.
upright.advice: Channel today's surge of energy into one bold action, then plan the step after it.

reversed.short: Check whether impatience is steering, or frustration is burning with nowhere to go.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the horse bolts or digs in its hooves. Energy turns impulsive, plans are abandoned half-made, and temper flares when things move slowly. Or the fire is blocked and smoulders as frustration. A pause to choose a direction, and a commitment to stay with it, gives that heat something to do.
reversed.love: Hot-and-cold pursuit confuses people; decide what you want before you sweep anyone up.
reversed.work: Rushing ahead without the team is causing rework; slow to the pace of the plan.
reversed.self: Irritability may be unused energy looking for an outlet; move your body and then decide.
reversed.advice: Before acting on an impulse, wait one hour and ask whether you would still do it.

element.name: Fire of Fire
element.gloss: Fire twice over: the suit at its hottest, quickest and least patient.

astrology.name: Sagittarius
astrology.gloss: Sagittarius is the adventurer: restless, optimistic and aiming at far horizons.

number.name: Knight
number.gloss: The Knight is the suit in motion, taking its energy out into the world on a quest.

questions: Where is your energy urging you to go, and what would give it staying power?
When has acting boldly served you well, and when has it cost you?

name: Queen of Wands
essence: Warmth that fills a room and makes others braver.
figure: A crowned queen in a red-and-gold gown sits at ease on a stone throne, a tall staff upright in her hand, with sunflowers crowding around her, a golden sun at her back and a black cat sitting watchfully at her side. She stands for confident warmth: charisma, independence and creative self-possession.

symbols.meaning: Vitality that turns toward the light and encourages everything nearby to do the same.
Her private, intuitive side; independence that needs no audience and no permission.
Creative power held steadily, as something she is entirely comfortable owning.
A natural radiance, the kind of presence people warm themselves beside.

upright.short: Express yourself with warm confidence and make room for other people's brilliance.
upright.meaning: The Queen of Wands is at home in her own skin. She favours showing up fully: expressing yourself with colour and conviction, hosting, encouraging and leading by enthusiasm. Her confidence is generous. She shines without needing anyone else to dim, and others tend to grow bolder in her company.
upright.love: Be warmly, unmistakably yourself, and take delight in a partner who is the same.
upright.work: Lead with enthusiasm and visible belief in the work; your energy sets the temperature.
upright.self: Wear, say or make the thing that feels most like you, without toning it down.
upright.advice: Offer one person sincere encouragement today, and accept some in return.

reversed.short: Notice confidence dimmed by comparison, or warmth tipping into needing the spotlight.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the fire wavers. Confidence gives way to comparison and you measure yourself against others, or warmth becomes a need to be the centre of every room. You may also be tired from keeping everyone else's spirits up. Returning to what you enjoy, unobserved, relights the flame from the inside.
reversed.love: Jealousy or a need for constant reassurance is asking you to tend your own self-regard.
reversed.work: You are dimming yourself to avoid standing out, or bristling when someone else shines.
reversed.self: Comparing your inner life with other people's highlights leaves you feeling smaller than you are.
reversed.advice: Do something creative purely for your own enjoyment, and show it to nobody.

element.name: Water of Fire
element.gloss: Water within fire: heat that is felt inwardly and given out as warmth and loyalty.

astrology.name: Aries
astrology.gloss: Aries gives her directness and courage: she begins things and says what she means.

number.name: Queen
number.gloss: The Queen masters her suit from within, embodying its quality instead of chasing it.

questions: Where do you shine most naturally, and do you allow yourself to be seen there?
Whose brilliance could you celebrate today without feeling that it takes from yours?

name: King of Wands
essence: A vision big enough for others to stand inside.
figure: A grey-bearded king in an ermine-trimmed robe and red mantle sits forward on his throne between two golden lions, holding a staff that has flowered with white lilies, a hill town and mountain behind him. He stands for mature leadership: bold vision joined to responsibility for those who follow it.

symbols.meaning: Authority that produces something living; leadership judged by what grows under it.
Courage and pride, seated calmly at either hand and fully under command.
The weight of office, a reminder that this rank comes with duties.
The community his decisions affect, kept in the picture and in mind.

upright.short: Turn a broad creative vision into generous, accountable leadership.
upright.meaning: The King of Wands leads from conviction. He sees where things could go and has the nerve to take people there. The card favours thinking big, deciding clearly and inspiring others by example. Its measure of success is generous: a good leader here answers for the outcome and shares the credit.
upright.love: Bring energy and initiative to the relationship, and make your loyalty obvious in action.
upright.work: Set the direction, communicate it vividly and take responsibility for how it lands.
upright.self: Trust your larger vision for your life enough to make one decision in its favour.
upright.advice: State your vision in a sentence, then ask someone affected by it what they need from you.

reversed.short: Look at where vision has become impatience, or leadership forgets who it serves.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the king's fire runs ahead of his judgement. Big talk outpaces delivery, impatience turns bossy, or the vision serves the leader's ego more than the people involved. It can also show a reluctance to lead when you are clearly the one to do it. Listening well is what steadies the crown.
reversed.love: Deciding for both of you is not the same as leading; ask before you announce.
reversed.work: Grand plans need follow-through; commit to less and deliver all of it.
reversed.self: You are either overriding everyone or doubting your right to take charge; neither is leadership.
reversed.advice: Ask for honest feedback on how you lead, and change one thing because of it.

element.name: Air of Fire
element.gloss: Air directing fire: enthusiasm given strategy, a plan and a persuasive voice.

astrology.name: Leo
astrology.gloss: Leo lends him presence, generosity and a ruler's pride in protecting his own.

number.name: King
number.gloss: The King governs the suit outwardly, turning its energy into decisions others rely on.

questions: What vision would you lead others toward if you fully trusted your own judgement?
Who depends on the choices you make, and how do you keep them in view?

name: Ace of Cups
essence: A cup so full that it has to be shared.
figure: A hand lowers from a cloud to steady a great golden chalice that overflows in bright streams into a lake dotted with water lilies, a sunburst behind it and a quiet lakeside town beyond. It stands for the heart opening: a fresh surge of feeling, compassion or creative love.

symbols.meaning: Feeling that exceeds its container, generous by nature and impossible to ration.
Emotion flowing outward into ordinary life, feeding whatever it reaches.
Something beautiful rooted in deep water; tenderness rising to the surface.
A gift being offered gently, to be received and not seized.

upright.short: Make space for a new feeling, creative connection or act of emotional openness.
upright.meaning: The Ace of Cups marks a beginning in the heart. A new affection, a creative flow or a wave of tenderness is welling up, and the card favours letting it. Openness is the whole instruction: receive what is being offered, feel it fully and allow it to spill over into kindness toward others.
upright.love: A new connection, or new warmth in an old one, is ready to be welcomed without holding back.
upright.work: Bring heart to the task; work you care about draws out your most imaginative side.
upright.self: Let yourself be moved by something today, and do not hurry to tidy the feeling away.
upright.advice: Tell someone, simply and directly, one thing you appreciate about them.

reversed.short: A feeling is held back or poured out without return; tend your own cup first.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the cup is tipped or tightly lidded. Feelings are being held in because expressing them seems risky, or you have given so much that nothing is left in the vessel. This is a call to turn some of that care inward. A cup that is refilled gently and often has something to offer again.
reversed.love: You are guarding your heart closely; consider one small, safe way to let warmth through.
reversed.work: Going through the motions without feeling is draining; find the part of the work you still care about.
reversed.self: The kindness you extend so readily to others is overdue in your own direction.
reversed.advice: Do one thing that refills you emotionally before you give anything more away.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is feeling, intuition and connection; this card is its clear first spring.

astrology.name: Water signs
astrology.gloss: Aces hold the whole element: Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces gathered in a single source.

number.gloss: One is the wellspring, the single point from which all the suit's feeling flows.

questions: What feeling is rising in you that deserves to be welcomed and not managed?
How do you refill your own cup, and when did you last do so?

name: Two of Cups
essence: Two cups raised, two people truly meeting.
figure: Two people face each other and lift matching golden cups, eyes level and smiling, beneath a staff twined with two snakes and crowned by a winged lion's head, with lilies and roses framing them. They stand for partnership at its best: mutual, chosen and balanced.

symbols.meaning: Equal exchange; each brings a full vessel and offers it freely to the other.
Meeting eye to eye, with neither person looking up to or down on the other.
An old emblem of exchange and healing: two different energies working as one.
Passion lifted by respect, strong feeling given dignity and direction.

upright.short: Meet another person with mutual respect; connection grows through honest exchange.
upright.meaning: The Two of Cups is about a real meeting between two people. It may be romantic, a friendship or a working alliance; what matters is that it runs both ways. The card favours honest exchange, in which each person offers something true and receives the same. Connection deepens through that give and take.
upright.love: Mutual attraction and respect are present; build on them by sharing something honest.
upright.work: A one-to-one partnership or agreement looks promising when the terms are fair to both.
upright.self: Offer yourself the respect you would give a valued partner, including in how you speak inwardly.
upright.advice: Ask someone important to you a real question, and listen fully to the answer.

reversed.short: Notice where an exchange has become uneven, and what honesty would rebalance it.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the cups are raised at different heights. One person gives more, words are being misheard, or a small rift has opened and is going unmentioned. The bond is seldom gone; it is out of balance. Saying plainly what you need, and asking the same of the other person, lets it level again.
reversed.love: One of you is doing most of the reaching; name it gently before it hardens into distance.
reversed.work: An agreement no longer feels fair to one side; revisit the terms openly.
reversed.self: You may be seeking in someone else an acceptance you have yet to offer yourself.
reversed.advice: Raise one small imbalance with the person concerned, starting from what you value in them.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is connection here: two currents meeting and running on together.

astrology.name: Venus in Cancer
astrology.gloss: Affection in a caring, protective sign: love that wants to nurture and be close.

number.gloss: Two is the pair, a balance made by two distinct parts choosing each other.

questions: Which of your relationships feels most mutual, and what makes it so?
What would you like to offer, and receive, in your closest partnership at present?

name: Three of Cups
essence: Three cups clinking, and laughter that carries.
figure: Three women in bright dresses lift their golden cups together in a toast, heads thrown back in laughter, beneath a trellis heavy with grapes and roses, a sunny town climbing the hill behind. They stand for friendship, celebration and the support of people who are glad you exist.

symbols.meaning: A shared toast: joy that depends on being together and grows with company.
Harvest and plenty, the sweetness that comes after a season of tending.
Unselfconscious delight, the ease of being among people you trust.
Affection in full bloom, the warmth of friendship given open expression.

upright.short: Friendship and shared joy offer support; let yourself belong to a community.
upright.meaning: The Three of Cups celebrates the company you keep. It favours gathering, toasting, collaborating and letting friends carry some of your joys and troubles. There is real nourishment in being part of a circle. The card invites you to turn up, join in and allow yourself to belong.
upright.love: Bring your relationship into your wider circle; shared friends and laughter strengthen it.
upright.work: Collaboration is going well; celebrate the group's success and enjoy the camaraderie.
upright.self: Reach out to the friends who make you feel most like yourself.
upright.advice: Arrange a small get-together, or simply message a friend to say you are thinking of them.

reversed.short: Notice where you feel on the edge of a circle, or where company has replaced closeness.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the toast rings a little hollow. You may feel left out of a group, find that socialising has become excess or gossip, or notice friendships drifting through neglect. Sometimes it simply marks a need for quiet after too much company. The question is which connections truly feed you.
reversed.love: Outside opinions or a busy social calendar are crowding out time for just the two of you.
reversed.work: Cliques or office chatter are getting in the way; keep your part straightforward and kind.
reversed.self: You are surrounded by people and still feel unseen; seek one honest conversation over ten light ones.
reversed.advice: Contact one friend you have drifted from and suggest something simple to do together.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is shared feeling here, poured from cup to cup among friends.

astrology.name: Mercury in Cancer
astrology.gloss: Communication in a homely, caring sign: warm talk among people who feel like family.

number.gloss: Three is a circle of company, where joy expands because it is passed around.

questions: Who are the people that leave you feeling lighter, and how often do you see them?
What would you like to celebrate, and with whom?

name: Four of Cups
essence: Three cups ignored, a fourth held out, and a faraway stare.
figure: A young person sits beneath a tree with chin propped on one hand, gazing off into the distance, three golden cups untouched on the grass. From the edge of the picture a hand offers a fourth cup, so far unnoticed. They stand for apathy and withdrawal, and for the offer that goes unseen.

symbols.meaning: A new possibility arriving from outside your line of sight while you look elsewhere.
What you already have, grown so familiar that it no longer registers.
Boredom or brooding; attention turned so far inward that it misses the present.
A comfortable place to sit things out, restful and also easy to stay in too long.

upright.short: Pause with a feeling of disinterest and notice an offer you may be overlooking.
upright.meaning: The Four of Cups describes a flat, inward mood. Nothing appeals, and what is on offer seems not quite right. Sometimes this is a healthy pause for reflection; sometimes it is discontent that keeps you from noticing something good. The card asks you to look up and take stock honestly.
upright.love: Taking a partner for granted, or dismissing interest too quickly, deserves a second look.
upright.work: Disengagement is a signal; ask whether you need rest, a challenge or a different direction.
upright.self: Sit with the restlessness long enough to learn what it wants, then glance around you.
upright.advice: Name three good things already within reach, and one offer you have not properly considered.

reversed.short: Look up from the mood you have been sitting in; an invitation is still within reach.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the figure lifts their head. A spell of disinterest is ending and you begin to notice what is being offered. Energy to take part returns. This can also show reluctance to leave a familiar sulk; if so, a single small yes is usually enough to break the stillness and get you moving.
reversed.love: You are ready to re-engage; respond to the gesture you previously let pass.
reversed.work: Motivation is returning; say yes to the opportunity while your curiosity is awake.
reversed.self: The fog of 'whatever' is thinning, and you can choose to take part again.
reversed.advice: Accept one invitation this week that you would normally decline out of habit.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is still and a little stagnant here, a pond waiting for a fresh current.

astrology.name: Moon in Cancer
astrology.gloss: Deep moods in the Moon's own sign: feelings turned inward, protective and private.

number.gloss: Four is stability, which in the heart can tip from contentment into standing still.

questions: What is being offered to you that your present mood has kept you from seeing?
Is your withdrawal giving you rest, or keeping you from something you want?

name: Five of Cups
essence: Three cups spilled, two still standing behind you.
figure: A figure wrapped in black sits hunched on rocks beside a river, face buried in both hands, with three golden cups overturned and spilling red in front and two more standing upright behind. A stone bridge crosses the water to the far bank. They stand for grief and regret, and the slow turn toward what remains.

symbols.meaning: What has been lost and cannot be gathered up again; the grief is for something real.
What is still whole, standing just behind the mourner and waiting to be noticed.
A way across to the other side, solid and open when the time comes to stand.
Mourning given its proper form; sorrow that is allowed to be seen.

upright.short: Acknowledge disappointment without letting what was lost hide what still remains.
upright.meaning: The Five of Cups honours sorrow. Something has gone badly or ended, and the feeling deserves room. The card favours letting yourself grieve without rushing toward a silver lining. It also keeps two full cups in the picture: in time, turning to what remains is part of how the heart mends.
upright.love: A disappointment needs acknowledging between you before either of you can move forward.
upright.work: A setback hurts; let yourself feel it, then look at what is still workable.
upright.self: Allow yourself to be sad about what did not work out, without arguing yourself out of it.
upright.advice: Give your disappointment a set time and your full attention, then name one thing that is left.

reversed.short: Grief is easing its grip; turn, when you are ready, toward the cups still standing.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the figure begins to turn round. The sharpest part of a loss has passed and you can start to see what survived it. Forgiveness, of yourself or someone else, becomes possible. If the sorrow has instead been pushed down unfelt, the card suggests giving it its due so that it can finally move.
reversed.love: You are ready to forgive, or to be forgiven, and let an old hurt take up less room.
reversed.work: Lessons from a failure are becoming usable; carry them over the bridge with you.
reversed.self: You can remember what happened without living inside it; that is what healing looks like.
reversed.advice: Do one thing today that belongs to what comes next and not to what was lost.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is sorrow here: feeling that has spilled and needs time to drain away.

astrology.name: Mars in Scorpio
astrology.gloss: Intense feeling in a sign of depth: emotions that cut keenly and then transform.

number.gloss: Five unsettles the comfortable four, bringing loss and with it a chance to grow.

questions: What loss are you still facing, and what would it mean to give it proper attention?
Which two cups are still standing behind you, waiting for you to turn round?

name: Six of Cups
essence: A cup of flowers, passed from hand to hand.
figure: In a walled courtyard overgrown with roses, a girl in a red headscarf hands a golden cup brimming with white blossom to a smiling, bearded man seated opposite her, and five more flower-filled cups stand in a row along the wall. They stand for simple kindness, memory and gifts given freely.

symbols.meaning: A gift with no strings attached, given for the pleasure of giving.
A sheltered, familiar place, like the safe corners of memory you can return to.
Good moments collected over time, kept where you can see and revisit them.
Old affection still in flower, rooted long ago and blooming now.

upright.short: A memory or familiar kindness can nourish you; bring its lesson into the present.
upright.meaning: The Six of Cups reaches back to what was good. A memory, an old friend, a childhood pleasure or an uncomplicated act of kindness has something to give you now. The card favours generosity without calculation and a gentle look at your roots, taking their sweetness forward instead of moving back in.
upright.love: Simple, thoughtful gestures say a great deal; revisit something you used to love doing together.
upright.work: An old contact, skill or idea turns out to be useful; kindness to colleagues is repaid.
upright.self: Reconnect with something you loved as a child and see what it still has to offer.
upright.advice: Give someone a small, unexpected kindness with no thought of what comes back.

reversed.short: Ask whether the past is nourishing you or keeping you from the present.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the courtyard gate needs opening. You may be idealising how things used to be, replaying old stories or measuring the present against a polished memory. Or you are ready to leave a childhood pattern behind. The past can be honoured and still left where it belongs, behind you.
reversed.love: Comparing a partner with someone from before, or with how things once were, is unfair to today.
reversed.work: 'How we have always done it' is holding things back; keep the lesson and update the method.
reversed.self: A younger version of you is still steering; thank them, and take the wheel as who you are today.
reversed.advice: Notice one way you are repeating an old pattern and try a different response once.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is memory here, a still pool reflecting earlier days.

astrology.name: Sun in Scorpio
astrology.gloss: Light brought into a deep, retentive sign: old feelings warmed and seen clearly.

number.gloss: Six is exchange and harmony: giving and receiving in easy balance.

questions: Which memory still nourishes you, and what does it remind you that you value?
Where might fondness for the past be keeping you from what is in front of you?

name: Seven of Cups
essence: Seven cups in the clouds, and only two hands.
figure: Seen from behind, a figure in a star-patterned robe raises a hand to their chin before seven golden cups floating in cloud, each holding a different vision: a castle, a serene face, a serpent, a laurel wreath, a jewelled crown, a heap of treasure and a dragon. They stand for imagination, wishing and the difficulty of choosing.

symbols.meaning: Many tempting options at once, all equally vivid while they stay in the air.
Daydream territory; nothing here has yet touched the ground of real life.
Wishes for status and wealth, attractive at a distance and untested up close.
Some fantasies have teeth; not every shining option is good for you.
The dreamer weighing it all up, undecided, drawn first one way and then another.

upright.short: Many appealing possibilities compete for attention; separate a wish from a workable choice.
upright.meaning: The Seven of Cups spreads out a feast of possibilities. Imagination is running freely, which is a pleasure and a creative resource. The difficulty is telling a workable option from a lovely mirage. The card favours dreaming widely and then bringing each wish down to earth to see what it actually asks of you.
upright.love: Check whether you are relating to a real person or to an idea of them you have built.
upright.work: Too many appealing directions are diluting your effort; test the most promising against the facts.
upright.self: Enjoy your daydreams and ask which of them you would truly want once the gloss wore off.
upright.advice: Pick one option from the cloud and write down the first practical step it would require.

reversed.short: The haze thins; choose one real option, or admit which wish was never yours.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the clouds begin to part. Fantasy gives way to a clearer view and a choice becomes possible. You may feel briefly deflated as some bright options turn out to be empty. Alternatively, the card shows paralysis among too many choices; narrowing to two and deciding between them breaks the spell.
reversed.love: Illusions about a relationship are clearing, and you can decide based on what is really there.
reversed.work: You are ready to commit to one path; let the others go without counting them as losses.
reversed.self: Being honest about what you truly want dissolves several distractions at a stroke.
reversed.advice: Cross three options off your list for good and notice the relief.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is imagination here, the shifting reflections that play on its surface.

astrology.name: Venus in Scorpio
astrology.gloss: Desire in a sign of intensity: powerful wants, not all of which are what they seem.

number.gloss: Seven tests discernment, asking you to sort what is real from what merely glitters.

questions: Which of your wishes would you still want if it arrived with all its ordinary costs?
What are you avoiding by keeping every option open?

name: Eight of Cups
essence: Eight cups left stacked; a path leading up into the dark.
figure: A traveller in a red cloak, staff in hand and pack on their back, walks away up a rocky path beneath a crescent moon toward snowy peaks, leaving eight golden cups neatly stacked on the stones behind. Nothing is broken or spilled. They stand for choosing to leave something that is no longer enough.

symbols.meaning: What was built with care and is still intact; leaving it is a choice, not a defeat.
A decision already made, attention given to the road ahead and not the pile behind.
A dim, honest light: enough to walk by when certainty is not available.
A harder road taken deliberately in search of something that matters more.

upright.short: Consider leaving an unfulfilling pattern even when it is familiar and hard to release.
upright.meaning: The Eight of Cups is the quiet decision to go. Nothing dramatic has happened; something simply stopped being enough, and you have noticed. It favours honouring that knowledge even when what you are leaving looks perfectly fine to others. The search for deeper meaning starts with a step into uncertainty.
upright.love: If your heart has already left, honesty is kinder than staying out of habit.
upright.work: A role that looks good on paper no longer fits; begin exploring what would feel meaningful.
upright.self: Trust the restlessness that tells you there is more for you than this.
upright.advice: Admit to yourself what no longer satisfies you, even if you are not ready to act on it.

reversed.short: Notice whether you are staying from fear or leaving too early to face a feeling.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the traveller pauses on the path. You may know something is finished and be unable to leave it, going back and forth without settling. Or you may be walking away from one thing after another so as not to face a discomfort that travels with you. Either way, the card asks what you are truly looking for.
reversed.love: You keep returning to a situation hoping it has changed; look at what is actually different.
reversed.work: One foot is out of the door and one is in; that half-commitment is costing you both ways.
reversed.self: Ask whether moving on would solve the feeling or only relocate it.
reversed.advice: Write down what you would need in order to stay wholeheartedly, and whether it is possible.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is the ebbing tide here, feeling that has drained out of a place.

astrology.name: Saturn in Pisces
astrology.gloss: Sober realism meeting a dreamy sign: admitting that a dream has run dry.

number.gloss: Eight is movement onward, the momentum that carries you beyond what you have outgrown.

questions: What have you outgrown that still looks fine from the outside?
What are you searching for that your present situation cannot give you?

name: Nine of Cups
essence: Nine cups in an arch, and a satisfied smile.
figure: A contented figure lounges on patterned cushions with one hand behind the head, eyes closed and smiling, beneath an arch of nine golden cups with fruit trees ripening above. Every line of the body says ease. They stand for satisfaction: wishes granted, comforts enjoyed and gratitude for both.

symbols.meaning: Achievements and pleasures arranged like a display, plentiful and proudly kept.
Rest that has been earned, with nothing left to prove this afternoon.
Contentment felt from the inside, needing nobody else to confirm it.
Plenty within easy reach; the good things here are real and meant to be tasted.

upright.short: Savour a personal satisfaction and ask what enough feels like on your own terms.
upright.meaning: The Nine of Cups is the card of personal satisfaction. Something you hoped for has come about, and the invitation is to enjoy it properly. It favours pleasure, gratitude and a relaxed pride in what you have. The deeper question is your own definition of enough, apart from anyone else's.
upright.love: Enjoy the affection you have; say out loud what makes you happy in it.
upright.work: A goal has been met; take satisfaction in it before setting the next.
upright.self: Let yourself feel pleased with your life as it stands, without adding a 'but'.
upright.advice: Savour one pleasure slowly today and name what it is that satisfies you.

reversed.short: Ask what enough means when getting what you wanted still leaves you restless.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the cups are full and the smile has slipped. You may have what you asked for and find it less fulfilling than expected, or be using comforts to cover a deeper hunger. Complacency can appear here as well. The remedy is a kind question: what would nourish you, as distinct from merely pleasing you?
reversed.love: Material or surface compatibility is in place, and something more heartfelt is being asked for.
reversed.work: Hitting the target has left you flat; revisit what you wanted the success to give you.
reversed.self: More of the same treat is not answering the need; ask what the craving stands in for.
reversed.advice: Swap one indulgence this week for something that leaves you feeling better afterwards.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is the brimming cup here: feeling at its fullest and most pleasurable.

astrology.name: Jupiter in Pisces
astrology.gloss: Generous abundance in a soulful sign: good fortune of the kind you can feel.

number.gloss: Nine is fulfilment for one, the personal harvest before it is shared in the ten.

questions: What does 'enough' feel like in your body, and when did you last notice it?
Which of your wishes, once granted, brought the satisfaction you expected?

name: Ten of Cups
essence: A rainbow of cups over people who chose each other.
figure: Friends and family sprawl on a lakeside lawn with a picnic of fruit, one strumming a guitar, a tan-and-white dog stretched out in front, and a rainbow strung with ten golden cups arches across the sky above them. They stand for shared happiness: belonging, harmony and love lived out in ordinary days.

symbols.meaning: Joy that arcs over everyone present; fulfilment as something held in common.
Harmony made together, each person adding to a tune that none could play alone.
Trust and ease; even the household animal feels entirely at home.
Everyday abundance, happiness built from simple shared meals and time.

upright.short: Shared emotional fulfilment grows through everyday care, belonging and chosen family.
upright.meaning: The Ten of Cups is emotional fulfilment in company. It shows the kind of happiness that rests on everyday care: people who turn up for one another, laugh easily and feel at home together. The card favours investing in those bonds, whether the family is one you were born into or one you gathered.
upright.love: A relationship feels like home; nurture it with small daily kindnesses and shared rituals.
upright.work: A team that truly gets along is a rare thing; value it and contribute to the goodwill.
upright.self: Notice where you belong without effort, and let yourself rest in it.
upright.advice: Spend unhurried time with the people who feel like home, with phones put away.

reversed.short: Notice where harmony is strained or performed, and what would make belonging real.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the rainbow is faint. There may be tension at home, a distance between people who love each other, or a picture of the perfect family that real life cannot match. Values may have drifted apart. Honest conversation about what each person needs does more for harmony than keeping up appearances.
reversed.love: You want different things from home life; talk about the picture each of you is holding.
reversed.work: Surface friendliness is covering unresolved friction; address it kindly and directly.
reversed.self: Comparing your people with an ideal keeps you from enjoying the imperfect closeness you have.
reversed.advice: Ask one person close to you what would help them feel more at home with you.

element.name: Water
element.gloss: Water is shared feeling here, a lake wide enough for everyone to gather beside.

astrology.name: Mars in Pisces
astrology.gloss: Energy poured into compassion: the active effort that goes into keeping people close.

number.gloss: Ten is completion shared, the suit's feeling brought to its fullest in community.

questions: Who feels like home to you, and how do you let them know?
What does harmony mean to you, as distinct from the absence of disagreement?

name: Page of Cups
essence: A fish jumps from the cup, and wonder follows.
figure: A young dreamer in a starry blue cloak sits on a rock by the sea and holds up a golden cup, from which a small fish leaps in a spray of water, to their evident surprise. They stand for the tender beginner in matters of the heart: imaginative, sensitive and open to the unexpected.

symbols.meaning: A surprise from the depths: an idea or feeling that arrives from nowhere and delights.
The heart held out with curiosity, ready to receive whatever turns up in it.
Imagination worn as everyday clothing; a dreamer's way of moving through the day.
A seat at the edge of deep feeling, close enough to listen without being swept off.

upright.short: Be curious about a tender feeling or surprising idea without dismissing it as naive.
upright.meaning: The Page of Cups invites you to take your feelings and fancies seriously, in a light-hearted way. A message from the heart, a creative whim or a gentle intuition is surfacing. The card favours curiosity over cynicism: listen to the odd idea, make the small sweet gesture, let yourself be touched.
upright.love: A shy, sincere gesture goes a long way; let yourself be a little soft.
upright.work: A playful, imaginative idea deserves a hearing before the practical objections arrive.
upright.self: Pay attention to dreams, doodles and passing feelings; they are telling you something.
upright.advice: Act on one small, kind impulse today without talking yourself out of it.

reversed.short: A tender feeling is hiding behind moodiness or daydream; give it honest words.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the fish slips back under. Feelings come out sideways as sulking or touchiness, or you drift into fantasy to avoid something real. Creativity may feel blocked by self-consciousness. The heart is still tender underneath. Giving the feeling plain, direct words is what lets it be received.
reversed.love: Hints and moods are doing the talking; say the vulnerable thing out loud instead.
reversed.work: Fear of looking foolish is keeping a good idea to yourself; share it in rough form.
reversed.self: You are being hard on your own sensitivity; treat it as a strength that needs care.
reversed.advice: Name what you are feeling in one honest sentence, to yourself or to someone kind.

element.name: Earth of Water
element.gloss: The earthy side of water: a feeling made small and tangible, like a note or a gift.

astrology.name: Water signs
astrology.gloss: This Page samples all three water signs, from Cancer's care to the dreaming of Pisces.

number.name: Page
number.gloss: The Page is the suit's student, meeting each emotion as if for the first time.

questions: What gentle impulse have you been dismissing as silly or naive?
How do you treat your own sensitivity: as a nuisance or as a source of insight?

name: Knight of Cups
essence: An offered cup, carried carefully across the water.
figure: A bearded rider in white with a blue cape guides a white horse at a calm walk through shallow water, one arm extended to hold out a golden cup as though presenting it. The pace is unhurried, almost ceremonial. The rider stands for the romantic and the idealist: someone who follows the heart and makes the offer.

symbols.meaning: An invitation or declaration held out in plain view, with all its sincerity.
Feeling that advances gently; this approach is graceful and never forced.
Moving through emotion while keeping your footing, touched and not submerged.
The colour of devotion and imagination, worn by one who leads with feeling.

upright.short: Express an invitation or ideal with sincerity, checking that action supports the romance.
upright.meaning: The Knight of Cups arrives with an offer: an invitation, a proposal, a creative venture or a heartfelt declaration. The card favours following what moves you and expressing it gracefully. Its test is follow-through. An ideal means most when action stands behind it, so let the gesture match the feeling.
upright.love: Make the romantic gesture, and back it up with consistent, everyday reliability.
upright.work: Pursue the project you believe in, and present it with warmth as well as logic.
upright.self: Let your ideals guide you, and give them practical legs to stand on.
upright.advice: Extend one sincere invitation today and be ready to act on it if it is accepted.

reversed.short: Check whether a lovely ideal is being lived out, or only admired from a distance.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the cup is offered and then withdrawn. Promises outrun delivery, moods shift with the tide, or a person or plan turns out to be more charming than dependable. You may be in love with an ideal and reluctant to meet the reality. Grounding a feeling in one concrete action shows what it is worth.
reversed.love: Sweet words without steady behaviour are being offered, by you or to you; look at the pattern.
reversed.work: An attractive proposal lacks substance; ask for specifics before you commit.
reversed.self: You are waiting to feel inspired before acting, when acting may be what brings the inspiration.
reversed.advice: Turn one thing you have promised or dreamed of into a dated, specific commitment.

element.name: Fire of Water
element.gloss: Fire meeting water: feeling stirred into motion and eager to declare itself.

astrology.name: Pisces
astrology.gloss: Pisces makes this knight a dreamer: compassionate, romantic and led by imagination.

number.name: Knight
number.gloss: The Knight takes the suit's quality out into the world, here as a quest of the heart.

questions: What ideal are you devoted to, and how does it show in what you actually do?
What invitation have you been meaning to extend, and what holds you back?

name: Queen of Cups
essence: A heart deep enough to hold what others bring to it.
figure: A crowned queen in a robe patterned like breaking waves sits on rocks at the sea's edge, bare feet in the surf, cradling an ornate lidded cup in both hands and gazing quietly to one side. She stands for emotional depth and compassion: someone who listens with her whole attention and trusts what she senses.

symbols.meaning: Feelings held with care and some privacy; her inner world is rich and protected.
In touch with emotion while seated on solid rock: moved, yet never carried off.
Someone so at home with feeling that she wears it as naturally as cloth.
Attention resting on something unseen, the look of a person listening inwardly.

upright.short: Listen compassionately to feelings while maintaining a boundary that protects your energy.
upright.meaning: The Queen of Cups feels deeply and stays steady. She favours listening with real attention, trusting intuition and offering comfort without trying to fix everything. Her compassion includes herself. She knows that a cup can be held out to others only when it is also protected, lidded and regularly refilled.
upright.love: Offer your full presence; being truly heard is one of the most loving things there is.
upright.work: Read the mood of the room and respond to what people need as well as what they say.
upright.self: Treat your feelings as trustworthy information, and give them quiet in which to speak.
upright.advice: Listen to someone today without advising, and afterwards do the same for yourself.

reversed.short: Notice where you are absorbing others' feelings and neglecting to protect your own.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the tide comes in over the rocks. You may be soaking up everyone else's emotions until you cannot tell which are yours, or giving care in the hope of being needed. Moods swing and the lid comes off. A firmer shoreline, a clear sense of where you end and others begin, restores your depth.
reversed.love: Looking after a partner's feelings at the cost of your own leaves you both adrift.
reversed.work: You are carrying colleagues' stress home with you; decide what is yours to hold.
reversed.self: Your emotions are flooding because they have had no steady outlet; give them one.
reversed.advice: Before saying yes to anyone's need, pause and ask what you need first.

element.name: Water of Water
element.gloss: Water twice over: feeling at its deepest, most receptive and most reflective.

astrology.name: Cancer
astrology.gloss: Cancer gives her a protective tenderness and a strong instinct for making others feel safe.

number.name: Queen
number.gloss: The Queen holds her suit inwardly, a quiet authority in everything to do with feeling.

questions: Whose feelings are you carrying that are not yours to carry?
What does your intuition tell you when you give it a quiet moment?

name: King of Cups
essence: Calm at the centre while the sea moves around you.
figure: A crowned, grey-bearded king in wave-blue robes sits on a stone throne set among rolling waves, a golden cup in one hand and a trident in the other, his expression composed. The water churns at his feet and he remains unmoved. He stands for emotional maturity: deep feeling paired with steady judgement.

symbols.meaning: Stability in the midst of strong emotion; he does not need calm water to stay seated.
Command over the tides of feeling, directing them instead of being tossed about.
Compassion held level; the cup does not spill, however rough the sea.
Feeling that is fully present and yet not in charge of the response.

upright.short: Respond to strong emotions with steadiness; care and clear judgement can work together.
upright.meaning: The King of Cups feels everything and is ruled by none of it. He favours responding instead of reacting: acknowledging strong emotion, yours or another's, and then choosing a considered course. This is the calm of a good counsellor or a kind diplomat, in whom care and clear judgement work together.
upright.love: Stay present and steady when feelings run high; your calm lets a partner feel safe.
upright.work: Handle a charged situation with tact, hearing every side before you decide.
upright.self: You can hold a strong emotion without being steered by it; give it a moment, then choose.
upright.advice: When something stirs you up today, name the feeling silently before you reply.

reversed.short: Look at where feelings are suppressed or spilling over, and what steadiness needs.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the sea gets into the throne room. Emotions are either bottled until they burst or allowed to run the show. Calm becomes coldness, or care becomes a way of steering people. The card asks for honest contact with what you feel, so that composure is real and not a lid screwed down tight.
reversed.love: Going quiet and distant when upset leaves a partner guessing; say what is going on.
reversed.work: Strained composure is leaking out as irritability; deal with the pressure at its source.
reversed.self: You have been telling yourself you are fine for a while; check whether that is still true.
reversed.advice: Share one feeling you have been holding in with someone you trust to hear it.

element.name: Air of Water
element.gloss: Air over water: strong feeling tempered by reflection and good counsel.

astrology.name: Scorpio
astrology.gloss: Scorpio gives him depth and control: powerful currents kept well beneath a calm surface.

number.name: King
number.gloss: The King governs outwardly, applying the suit's wisdom on behalf of other people.

questions: How do you stay steady when the people around you are in turmoil?
Which feeling have you been managing so well that you have stopped listening to it?

name: Ace of Swords
essence: One clean cut through the fog.
figure: A hand rises from the clouds holding a sword point-upward, its tip passing through a golden crown hung with an olive branch and a white lily, while rays of light fan out behind. It stands for mental clarity and truth: the single sharp insight that changes how a whole matter is seen.

symbols.meaning: A clear thought held steady, precise enough to separate what is true from what is not.
Clarity as a kind of sovereignty; to see truly is to regain command of your mind.
Truth can serve peace and good faith, and does not have to be used as a weapon.
Understanding breaking through after a spell of confusion.

upright.short: A clear idea cuts through confusion; use honesty precisely and with care.
upright.meaning: The Ace of Swords is a moment of seeing clearly. A new idea, an honest realisation or the right question cuts through muddle and shows you what you are dealing with. It favours naming things accurately and deciding on that basis. The blade has two edges, so handle the truth with precision and with care.
upright.love: Say the true thing kindly and plainly; clarity is a form of respect.
upright.work: Define the problem in one exact sentence, and the solution becomes much easier to find.
upright.self: A realisation about yourself is arriving; let it be clear before you decide what to do with it.
upright.advice: Write the plain truth of your situation in a single sentence, with no softening.

reversed.short: Thinking is clouded or a truth is being used carelessly; slow down and define terms.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the blade is dulled or pointing the wrong way. Thinking gets tangled, facts are missing, or an insight is delivered so sharply that it wounds instead of helping. You may be forcing a decision before the fog lifts. Gathering one more fact and choosing your words carefully restores the edge.
reversed.love: Being right is being put ahead of being understood; ask before you assert.
reversed.work: A decision is being made on assumptions; check the key fact that everything else rests on.
reversed.self: Your mind is going in circles; get the thoughts onto paper where you can see them.
reversed.advice: Pause the debate and ask, 'What do we actually know?' before going any further.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is thought, language and truth; this card is its first clear breath.

astrology.name: Air signs
astrology.gloss: Aces hold their element entire: Gemini, Libra and Aquarius in one pure principle.

number.gloss: One is the single point, an idea in its sharpest and most undivided form.

questions: What truth, stated plainly, would clear the air in your present situation?
Where could one precise question save you a great deal of confusion?

name: Two of Swords
essence: Blindfolded between two blades, holding the balance.
figure: A blindfolded woman sits on rocks at the edge of a night sea, two long swords crossed over her chest and a crescent moon above her. Her arms are steady and so is her breathing. She stands for stalemate and suspended choice: holding two options in balance while refusing, for the moment, to look.

symbols.meaning: A choice not to see, whether to concentrate inwardly or to avoid what is in view.
Two equal arguments held in tension, guarding the heart behind them.
Feelings kept at her back, present and moving even while they go unconsulted.
Only partial light; the full picture has not yet come into view.

upright.short: A difficult choice needs information as well as quiet; postponing it also has a cost.
upright.meaning: The Two of Swords is a deliberate pause before a difficult choice. Both options have weight, and you are holding them level while you think. That stillness can be wise. It also takes effort, and it cannot last for ever. The card favours gathering what you need to know, then lowering the blindfold.
upright.love: An unspoken stand-off is keeping the peace and the distance; one of you needs to speak first.
upright.work: You are stuck between two reasonable options; find the missing fact that would tip the scale.
upright.self: Notice what you are choosing not to look at, and whether that still protects you.
upright.advice: List what you would need to know in order to decide, and go and find one of those things.

reversed.short: A stalemate is ending; look at what you have avoided seeing, then choose.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the arms tire and the blindfold slips. Information you were avoiding comes into view, and the balance has to tip one way. This can feel like relief or like being flooded by everything you had held off. Taking the feelings into account, and not only the arguments, helps the decision settle.
reversed.love: What went unsaid is coming out; let it, and listen as well as defend.
reversed.work: The decision can no longer be deferred; choose with what you have and adjust afterwards.
reversed.self: You already lean one way; admitting it is most of the choosing.
reversed.advice: Flip a coin, and pay attention to which result you find yourself hoping for.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is thought held perfectly still here, the mind balancing two ideas at once.

astrology.name: Moon in Libra
astrology.gloss: Feeling in the sign of the scales: a deep wish for peace that hesitates to tip the balance.

number.gloss: Two is opposition in equilibrium, a pair of forces pausing before either one moves.

questions: What are you avoiding looking at because seeing it would force a decision?
If both options were taken away, which would you miss more?

name: Three of Swords
essence: An honest ache, with light around its edges.
figure: A bright red heart hangs against storm clouds and slanting rain, pierced through by three swords, and a halo of light glows around it all the same. No person appears: this is feeling itself. It stands for heartache named truthfully, the kind of sorrow that begins to ease once it is acknowledged.

symbols.meaning: A hurt that reached the centre; some truths are felt before they can be thought.
Words, facts or realisations that cut, each one clear and difficult to deny.
Release: tears and weather that wash the air and let the pressure fall.
Even while hurting, the heart stays alight; pain is evidence of how much it cares.

upright.short: Name a painful truth and allow yourself care rather than explaining the hurt away.
upright.meaning: The Three of Swords names a hurt. Something true has landed hard: a disappointment, a separation or words that stung. The card does not ask you to be brave about it. It favours letting the feeling be what it is, saying it out loud and treating yourself gently while the weather passes through.
upright.love: A hurt between you needs saying plainly and hearing fully before it can start to mend.
upright.work: Criticism or a letdown has stung; allow that it hurts before you look for the lesson.
upright.self: Let yourself cry or be quiet for a while; this is how the heart clears, and there is no weakness in it.
upright.advice: Put your hurt into honest words, on paper or to a kind listener, without explaining it away.

reversed.short: An old hurt is ready to be tended; release what you have kept pressed down.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the swords begin to loosen. A hurt you have carried is ready to ease, and forgiveness or simple acceptance becomes possible. If the pain has instead been pressed down and never felt, the card invites you to let it surface gently, in good company, so that mending can start in earnest.
reversed.love: You are ready to stop rehearsing an old injury; say what you need in order to let it rest.
reversed.work: A past disappointment is losing its sting, and you can approach similar work without flinching.
reversed.self: Be patient with the tender place; it is closing over at its own pace.
reversed.advice: Do one gentle thing for the part of you that was hurt, as you would for a friend.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is words and truths here, and the way a clear thought can pierce the heart.

astrology.name: Saturn in Libra
astrology.gloss: Hard reality meeting a sign of relationship: an honest reckoning in matters of the heart.

number.gloss: Three brings something into the open; here it is a feeling that can no longer stay hidden.

questions: Which hurt have you been explaining away when it only needs to be felt?
What would you say to a dear friend who was carrying the ache that you carry?

name: Four of Swords
essence: Swords hung up; the mind lies down.
figure: A sleeper lies curled on a stone bed in a quiet chapel, head pillowed on one arm, with three swords hung neatly on the wall, a fourth laid along the bed's edge and soft light falling through a stained-glass window on to white lilies. They stand for rest and recovery after strain.

symbols.meaning: Worries and arguments set aside for now, still there and no longer in your hands.
One matter kept close, to be picked up again once you are rested.
Quiet, coloured light; a sheltered space where the outside world is filtered.
Peace and renewal, fresh growth keeping watch while you recover.

upright.short: Rest and mental distance are part of recovery; leave space before your next response.
upright.meaning: The Four of Swords prescribes a pause. After conflict, effort or mental strain, the mind needs quiet before it can think well again. The card favours sleep, solitude and stepping back from the fray. This is preparation and not avoidance: the sword is beside the bed, and you take it up again when you are ready.
upright.love: Give a tense subject a rest and return to it when you are both calmer.
upright.work: Take the break; your next good idea is waiting on the far side of proper rest.
upright.self: Protect a stretch of quiet time as firmly as you would an important appointment.
upright.advice: Cancel one non-essential thing and use the space to do nothing whatsoever.

reversed.short: Notice whether you are restless inside a needed pause, or resting past its purpose.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the rest is being disturbed. You may be pushing on when you badly need to stop, unable to switch off even lying down. Or a period of withdrawal has gone on so long that it has turned to stagnation, and getting up is overdue. The card asks you to be honest about which applies to you.
reversed.love: Avoiding a conversation for the sake of peace has gone on long enough; return to it gently.
reversed.work: Running on empty is making simple things hard; rest is the productive option here.
reversed.self: Your body is asking to stop and your mind keeps overruling it; let the body win this one.
reversed.advice: Decide whether you need to lie down or to get up, and do that one thing today.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is the quieted mind here, thought allowed to settle like dust in a still room.

astrology.name: Jupiter in Libra
astrology.gloss: Generous ease in a sign of balance: the relief of a truce and a chance to recover.

number.gloss: Four is rest and structure, a stable enclosure in which to recover your strength.

questions: What would real rest look like for you, as distinct from merely stopping work?
Which worry could you hang on the wall for a while, knowing that it will keep?

name: Five of Swords
essence: All five swords in one pair of arms, and nobody left on the beach.
figure: A figure in a black coat lined with red stands on a beach with five swords gathered in folded arms, eyes lowered, while two others walk away along the shoreline with their backs turned and gulls wheel overhead. The figure stands for the hollow win: a conflict where victory costs more than it pays.

symbols.meaning: Everything won and nobody to share it with; the prize of a fight taken too far.
The relationships that a hard-won argument can cost, leaving without looking back.
Second thoughts arriving after the triumph, a win that does not feel like one.
Life going on regardless, unmoved by who came out on top.

upright.short: Winning an argument can damage connection; consider the price of being right.
upright.meaning: The Five of Swords looks at what happens after you win. Someone has come out on top of a dispute, and the atmosphere is sour. The card asks whether being right was worth what it damaged. It favours examining your tactics and your motives honestly, and choosing the relationship over the scoreboard where you can.
upright.love: Point-scoring in an argument leaves both of you lonelier; ask what you actually want to protect.
upright.work: A win that alienates colleagues is expensive; consider how you could repair the ground.
upright.self: Notice the part of you that needs the last word, and what it is afraid of losing.
upright.advice: In your next dispute, ask yourself what you want to be true an hour after it ends.

reversed.short: Lay down a fight that costs more than it gives, and repair what you can.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the swords are set down in the sand. A wish to make peace appears, or at least a weariness with fighting. Apology and repair become possible. If resentment still simmers, though, the card warns that an unresolved quarrel tends to return; real resolution needs each side to feel heard.
reversed.love: One of you can end the stand-off by apologising for your own part, without waiting to be asked.
reversed.work: An old rivalry has stopped serving anyone; offer a practical way to move on.
reversed.self: Replaying an argument you lost, or won, keeps you standing on that beach; walk on.
reversed.advice: Reach out to someone you clashed with and acknowledge one thing they were right about.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is sharp words here, argument used to win instead of to understand.

astrology.name: Venus in Aquarius
astrology.gloss: Affection in a cool, detached sign: principle placed above warmth, at a price.

number.gloss: Five is conflict and instability, the moment a settled pattern breaks into contest.

questions: Which argument did you win that you would now gladly trade for the friendship?
What matters more to you in this conflict: being right or being close?

name: Six of Swords
essence: Calmer water ahead, and the swords come too.
figure: A ferryman in a red hood poles a wooden boat across still water toward a sunlit town on the far shore, three passengers huddled under cloaks in the stern and six swords standing upright in the bow. Nobody speaks. They stand for transition: leaving difficulty behind and moving steadily toward relief.

symbols.meaning: A vessel for crossing over; you are between two shores, carried and not yet arrived.
Steady help, whether a guide, a friend or your own practical side doing the work.
Lessons and memories travel with you; they are cargo now and no longer wounds.
Smoother conditions in the direction you are heading, already visible from here.

upright.short: A gradual transition carries lessons from a difficult place toward a calmer one.
upright.meaning: The Six of Swords is a quiet departure from a hard place. Things are not joyful yet, and they are moving the right way. The card favours accepting help, travelling light and trusting a gradual crossing. You take the understanding you gained along with you; that is what the swords in the boat are for.
upright.love: A difficult period is easing; keep moving gently toward calmer ways of being together.
upright.work: A change of role, team or approach takes you somewhere more workable; let the shift take its time.
upright.self: You are in between, and that is a real place; be patient with the middle of the river.
upright.advice: Accept one offer of help with a transition you have been trying to manage alone.

reversed.short: Ask what keeps the boat tied up: unfinished feeling, or reluctance to accept help.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the boat stays at the jetty or keeps turning back. You know a move is needed and cannot quite make it, held by unfinished business or uncertainty about the far shore. Sometimes the load is too heavy to push off with. Deciding what truly needs to come with you makes the crossing possible.
reversed.love: You keep circling back to the same rough water; ask what would have to change for the trip to end.
reversed.work: A needed change is being delayed; identify the one thing you are waiting for and question it.
reversed.self: You are trying to cross with everything on board; set down the grievance that weighs most.
reversed.advice: Name one thing you are bringing from the old situation that could be left on the bank.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is perspective here, the clearer thinking that comes with distance from trouble.

astrology.name: Mercury in Aquarius
astrology.gloss: A clear, objective mind in a forward-looking sign: thinking your way to a better place.

number.gloss: Six restores equilibrium after the strife of five, a passage back toward peace.

questions: What are you in the middle of leaving, and what do you hope lies on the other shore?
Which lessons are worth carrying across, and which weights could stay behind?

name: Seven of Swords
essence: Tiptoeing out of camp with an armful of blades.
figure: A red-hooded figure slips away from a camp of tents at night, five swords bundled in their arms and a wary glance thrown over one shoulder, while two more swords stand stuck in the ground beside a small fire. A crescent moon watches. They stand for strategy and stealth, and the fine line between cleverness and deceit.

symbols.meaning: Taking what you can carry by wit instead of by force; resourcefulness with an edge.
The plan is incomplete; something has been overlooked or could not be managed alone.
An uneasy conscience, or simple caution, knowing this may not go unnoticed.
Other people unaware of what is happening, which is the heart of the ethical question.

upright.short: Consider discretion and strategy while checking where avoidance becomes dishonesty.
upright.meaning: The Seven of Swords is about acting quietly and independently. Sometimes that is wise: not every plan needs announcing, and a clever sidestep can beat a head-on fight.
