The card also asks an honest question. Where does discretion end and evasion begin, and would you be at ease if your methods were seen?
upright.love: Keeping something back may feel protective, yet secrecy tends to erode trust; weigh what to share.
upright.work: Think strategically and guard your plans, while staying on the right side of fair dealing.
upright.self: Notice where you are getting round a problem cleverly instead of facing it.
upright.advice: Ask of your current plan: would I be comfortable explaining this to everyone it affects?

reversed.short: Look at what you are hiding or sidestepping, and what coming clean would free.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the figure hesitates at the edge of the camp. A secret is surfacing, a shortcut has stopped working, or your own conscience is asking for a different approach. You may be the one deceived, or deceiving yourself. Bringing things into the open is uncomfortable, and it lightens the load.
reversed.love: A half-truth is weighing on you; an honest conversation now is easier than a discovery later.
reversed.work: The workaround is unravelling; return to the direct route and involve the people you bypassed.
reversed.self: A convenient story has been doing the rounds in your head; look at the part it leaves out.
reversed.advice: Own up to one small evasion, to yourself or another, and notice the relief that follows.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is cleverness here, the quick mind that plans three moves ahead.

astrology.name: Moon in Aquarius
astrology.gloss: Feeling in a detached, independent sign: instinct that prefers to act alone and unobserved.

number.gloss: Seven tests integrity, asking whether your methods match your principles.

questions: Where are you being strategic, and where have you slid into avoiding honesty?
What would you do differently if you knew that everyone could see your approach?

name: Eight of Swords
essence: Bound and blindfolded, with the path lying open behind.
figure: A blindfolded woman in a white dress stands wrapped in loops of red cloth among eight swords planted upright in the ground. Behind her a pale stone path winds freely away to the hills, and the swords leave wide gaps on every side. She stands for feeling trapped by thoughts when the way out is nearer than it seems.

symbols.meaning: Not seeing the options that exist; the limit lies in the view and not in the world.
Restrictions that are wound loosely and could be worked free with patience.
The barrier is incomplete; there is room to walk out once you look for it.
A clear way forward directly behind her, waiting to be noticed.

upright.short: A limiting story can make choices feel invisible; examine one constraint you can test.
upright.meaning: The Eight of Swords describes a mental cage. You feel hemmed in, short of options and unable to move, and much of that comes from the story you are telling about the situation. The card takes the feeling seriously and gently questions the facts. Testing a single assumption is often enough to find the gap.
upright.love: Believing there is nothing you can say keeps you silent; try one honest sentence.
upright.work: You feel boxed in by rules or expectations; check which ones are real and which you assumed.
upright.self: The thought 'I have no choice' deserves examining; list the options you ruled out too quickly.
upright.advice: Pick one limit you take for granted and test, in a small way, whether it actually holds.

reversed.short: The bindings are loosening; test one assumed limit and take the open path.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the blindfold comes off. You begin to see that some of the bars were made of belief, and options reappear. Taking back your own agency can feel unfamiliar after a long time stuck. If you still feel trapped, the card suggests asking who or what profits from your believing there is no way out.
reversed.love: You are finding your voice again; use it to ask for what you need.
reversed.work: A restriction you accepted turns out to be negotiable; ask the question.
reversed.self: You are kinder to yourself than you were, and with that kindness the cage has less hold.
reversed.advice: Take one small action you had told yourself was impossible, simply to see what happens.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is anxious thought here, the mind tying itself in knots of its own making.

astrology.name: Jupiter in Gemini
astrology.gloss: Expansive thinking in a restless sign: so many thoughts that they tangle and bind.

number.gloss: Eight is repetition, here a thought loop that keeps circling until it is interrupted.

questions: Which 'I can't' in your life have you never actually tested?
If a friend were in your position, what way out would you point to?

name: Nine of Swords
essence: Awake at three, with every worry on the wall.
figure: A woman sits up in bed in the dark, blue blanket gathered around her and one hand pressed to her forehead, while nine swords hang in a row on the wall behind. Nothing in the room is actually touching her. She stands for anxiety and sleepless worry: the mind at night, making everything larger.

symbols.meaning: Worries lined up overhead; they hang there, and not one of them has fallen.
The ache of overthinking; this trouble lives chiefly in the mind.
Night-time thinking, when problems lose their true size and no one is awake to ask.
Comfort close at hand, a reminder that care is nearer than the worry suggests.

upright.short: Anxious thoughts can grow in isolation; separate what is known from what is feared.
upright.meaning: The Nine of Swords is the card of the long night. Thoughts loop, regrets replay and worst cases multiply in the dark. The distress is real even where the dangers are not. The card favours gentleness and daylight: write the worries down, tell someone, and sort what is known from what is merely imagined.
upright.love: A private worry about the relationship grows in silence; share it and see what remains.
upright.work: Dread about a task is worse than the task; begin with its smallest piece.
upright.self: Be as kind to your anxious mind as you would be to a child woken by a bad dream.
upright.advice: Write down every worry, then mark which you can act on tomorrow and which you cannot.

reversed.short: Worry is loosening; share the thought you have carried alone and check its size.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the first grey light arrives. Anxiety begins to ease as you speak about it, or as the thing you dreaded proves manageable. The card can also show worry that is being hidden behind a capable face. In either case the direction is the same: out of isolation and toward someone who can listen.
reversed.love: Letting a partner see that you are struggling brings you closer than coping silently.
reversed.work: The problem looks smaller now that you have looked straight at it; take the next step.
reversed.self: You are learning that a thought is not a fact, and the nights are getting quieter.
reversed.advice: Tell one person what has been keeping you awake, and ask only that they listen.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is the racing mind here, thoughts multiplying in the quiet hours.

astrology.name: Mars in Gemini
astrology.gloss: Agitated energy in a busy-minded sign: thoughts that spar with one another all night.

number.gloss: Nine is intensity near its peak, the build-up that comes just before a release.

questions: Which of your worries is based on something known, and which on something imagined?
Who could you tell about what keeps you awake, and what stops you?

name: Ten of Swords
essence: The longest night ends; the sun is already coming up.
figure: A figure in a red cloak sits on a rock with their back to us, facing a sunrise that spreads gold across the horizon, while ten swords fan out in the dark sky above like the last of the night. The figure is whole and upright. This stands for a hard chapter reaching its end, and the first light after.

symbols.meaning: A difficulty at its fullest extent, now behind and above you instead of ahead.
The turn that follows a low point; morning arrives without being earned.
Rest after an ordeal, upright and intact, taking a moment before standing.
Night giving way; the worst of the weather has already passed over.

upright.short: An exhausting chapter has reached its limit; acknowledge the ending and begin recovery.
upright.meaning: The Ten of Swords marks the end of something draining. A situation has gone as far as it can, and there is an odd relief in that: nothing more needs to be endured or defended. The card favours accepting that this chapter is over, resting, and letting the new day arrive in its own time.
upright.love: A painful pattern has run its course; acknowledge the ending and let recovery begin.
upright.work: This job, task or arrangement has gone as far as it can; stop pouring effort in and review where you stand.
upright.self: The tiredness goes deeper than you have let on; you are allowed to stop and simply watch the sun rise.
upright.advice: Say aloud, 'This part is over,' and do one restful thing before making any plans.

reversed.short: Recovery has begun; stop replaying the ending and let the morning arrive.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the figure begins to stand. The lowest point is behind you and strength is returning, slowly and unevenly. Or you may be holding on to a finished situation, replaying it and unable to accept that it has closed. Either way the sun keeps rising. Small routines and patience carry the recovery along.
reversed.love: You are mending; resist reopening the story to check whether it still hurts.
reversed.work: Lessons from what ended are becoming clear, and they are the start of something sounder.
reversed.self: Getting up again is slow work; count each ordinary day as progress.
reversed.advice: Choose one small routine that marks a new start and repeat it every morning this week.

element.name: Air
element.gloss: Air is thought taken to its limit here, a story that has finally run out.

astrology.name: Sun in Gemini
astrology.gloss: Daylight entering a sign of the mind: clarity dawning after the long mental night.

number.gloss: Ten is the full measure, the end of the suit's road and the turn toward a new one.

questions: What has truly ended in your life, and what would help you to accept that?
What is the first small sign of morning that you can see from where you sit?

name: Page of Swords
essence: A sharp eye, a raised blade and a hundred questions.
figure: A young person stands on a rocky hilltop with a sword lifted high in one hand, red scarf snapping in the wind, eyes fixed alertly on something off to the side, mountains ranged behind. They stand for the curious, watchful mind: quick to question, keen to learn and still practising how to handle the blade.

symbols.meaning: A new idea held up to test it against the light; eagerness to prove a point.
A mind in motion, thoughts streaming quickly and changing with the breeze.
Vigilance and curiosity: always watching, noticing and gathering information.
A vantage point; thinking clearly needs a little height above the detail.

upright.short: Ask careful questions and test an intriguing idea before treating it as a fact.
upright.meaning: The Page of Swords is hungry to understand. Questions come quickly and so do opinions. The card favours learning, research and honest enquiry: asking why, checking sources and trying ideas out in conversation. Its growing edge is patience. A new idea is worth testing before you swing it about as fact.
upright.love: Ask curious questions and listen to the answers; interest is a form of affection.
upright.work: Research, fact-check and speak up with your questions; a fresh eye spots what others miss.
upright.self: Feed your mind something new and enjoy the stretch of not yet understanding it.
upright.advice: Ask one sincere 'why?' today in a place where you would normally nod along.

reversed.short: Curiosity has turned to gossip or haste; check a claim before you repeat it.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the blade is waved about carelessly. Words come out before they are thought through, curiosity slides into prying, or cleverness is used to score points. There can be plenty of talk and little action. Slowing down, checking facts and speaking with care gives the bright mind real value.
reversed.love: Sharp or sarcastic remarks are landing harder than you intend; say what you feel instead.
reversed.work: An unverified assumption is spreading; confirm it before it does any damage.
reversed.self: Your mind is busy and unfocused; choose one question and follow it properly.
reversed.advice: Before sharing a piece of news or an opinion, ask yourself whether it is true, kind and useful.

element.name: Earth of Air
element.gloss: Air brought to earth: ideas pinned down into facts that can be checked.

astrology.name: Air signs
astrology.gloss: Gemini, Libra and Aquarius all teach this student; none of them claims the card outright.

number.name: Page
number.gloss: The Page is the apprentice, learning to handle the suit's tools with growing skill.

questions: What are you genuinely curious about at present, and how could you learn more?
Where might you be speaking before you have checked what you know?

name: Knight of Swords
essence: A thought at full gallop, sword-first.
figure: A rider in a red cape leans forward over the neck of a galloping white horse, sword thrust out ahead and jaw set, stones flying from the hooves and clouds racing behind. Everything aims at a single point. The rider stands for the driven intellect: fast, direct and committed to the argument.

symbols.meaning: An idea used as a spearhead; the point is made before anyone else has finished speaking.
Thought at speed, covering ground quickly and with little room for turning.
What is kicked up or knocked aside by a charge that looks only forward.
Total conviction; doubt has been left behind at the starting line.

upright.short: Pursue a clear argument with courage, pausing long enough to notice who may be affected.
upright.meaning: The Knight of Swords goes straight at things. This card favours decisive action, frank speech and following a clear line of reasoning to its conclusion. It is excellent for cutting through dithering. Its blind spot is everything to either side, so glance up now and then to see who and what you are riding past.
upright.love: Be direct about what you think and feel, and leave space for a slower reply.
upright.work: Drive the idea forward with energy, and check that the team is still with you.
upright.self: Use your clarity to act, while staying open to being wrong on a detail.
upright.advice: Make your case clearly, then stop and ask, 'What am I missing?'

reversed.short: Speed or bluntness is outrunning judgement; rein in and look at who is nearby.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the charge loses its aim. Haste leads to mistakes, bluntness wounds, and energy is spent arguing for its own sake. You might be rushing to avoid thinking something through, or have run so hard that you are exhausted. Reining in, even briefly, lets judgement catch up with speed.
reversed.love: Winning the debate is costing warmth; slow down and ask how your words are landing.
reversed.work: Acting before the plan is clear is creating rework; take ten minutes to think it through.
reversed.self: Your thoughts are racing ahead of your wellbeing; give your mind a slower gait.
reversed.advice: Count to five before you answer today, particularly when you feel most certain.

element.name: Fire of Air
element.gloss: Fire driving air: an idea set alight and ridden hard toward its target.

astrology.name: Gemini
astrology.gloss: Gemini makes this knight quick-witted, talkative and restless for the next idea.

number.name: Knight
number.gloss: The Knight puts the suit into action, carrying its ideas out at full tilt.

questions: When has your directness helped you, and when has it lost you allies?
What might you notice if you slowed your pace by half for a single day?

name: Queen of Swords
essence: Clear eyes, an open hand and nothing left unsaid.
figure: A silver-haired queen in a robe of midnight blue and stars sits upright on a carved stone throne, a sword held vertically in her right hand and her left hand open and extended, with a falcon perched at her shoulder. She stands for hard-won clarity: honesty, independence and judgement tempered by experience.

symbols.meaning: Truth held straight, without tilt or flourish, as a standard to measure against.
An invitation to speak plainly, with fairness offered alongside the blade.
Sharp sight and independence; a mind that sees far and hunts for what is true.
Experience; her clear view was earned through what she has lived.

upright.short: Speak with discerning honesty and firm boundaries without losing your compassion.
upright.meaning: The Queen of Swords sees clearly and says so. She favours honest communication, firm boundaries and decisions made with a cool head. Her directness is a form of respect: she assumes you can handle the truth. Behind the blade is an open hand, so her clarity leaves room for compassion.
upright.love: Speak honestly about what you need and where your limits lie; clarity is kind.
upright.work: Give straightforward feedback and make the call on the facts, without softening them into mush.
upright.self: Trust your own perception, including when it tells you something uncomfortable.
upright.advice: State one boundary today in a single calm sentence, without justifying it.

reversed.short: Notice where honesty has gone cold or guarded, and let compassion back in.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the open hand closes. Clarity hardens into criticism, boundaries become walls, or old hurt sharpens your tongue. It can also show the reverse: emotion clouding your usual good judgement. The card asks you to let some warmth back into your honesty, and some honesty into your feelings.
reversed.love: Keeping someone at a distance with wit or criticism protects you and leaves you lonely.
reversed.work: Feedback has turned cutting; say what would help and not only what is wrong.
reversed.self: You are judging yourself by a standard you would never apply to a friend.
reversed.advice: Before offering a criticism, find one true and appreciative thing to say first.

element.name: Water of Air
element.gloss: Water within air: thought informed by feeling and seasoned by experience.

astrology.name: Libra
astrology.gloss: Libra gives her a commitment to fairness, weighing each side before she speaks.

number.name: Queen
number.gloss: The Queen has made the suit her own, wielding its clarity with inner authority.

questions: Where do you need to be more honest, and where more gentle with that honesty?
Which boundary, clearly stated, would make your life simpler?

name: King of Swords
essence: The considered verdict of a mind that has heard every side.
figure: A crowned, grey-bearded king sits on a stone throne before snow-covered peaks, chin resting on one hand in thought, the other hand on a sword set point-down before him, while two butterflies drift nearby. He stands for intellectual authority: reason, principle and the responsibility of deciding fairly.

symbols.meaning: Power at rest; the blade is ready and he reaches for thought before force.
Deliberation, the habit of weighing a matter fully before pronouncing on it.
Thoughts transformed and set free, lightness that sits alongside his gravity.
A cool, elevated view, high above the heat of the moment.

upright.short: Use knowledge and fair principles to make a clear, responsible decision.
upright.meaning: The King of Swords decides with his head. He favours logic, evidence and consistent principles, and he states his conclusions without drama. This is the card of good counsel and sound judgement. Its best expression uses expertise in the service of fairness, treating every person by the same clear rules.
upright.love: Talk a problem through calmly and fairly; clear agreements prevent a great deal of hurt.
upright.work: Make the decision on evidence and principle, explain your reasoning and stand by it.
upright.self: Step back from the feeling for a moment and ask what the facts support.
upright.advice: Set out the facts, the principle and the decision in that order before you act.

reversed.short: Check whether reason is serving fairness, or being used to control and dismiss.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the sword leaves the ground too readily. Logic is used to dominate, rules are applied without mercy, or a clever argument covers a self-serving motive. It may equally show muddled judgement and a reluctance to decide. Reason works best alongside humility and some regard for those it affects.
reversed.love: Being coolly correct is shutting down a partner's feelings; acknowledge them before you reason.
reversed.work: Authority is being exercised without listening; invite the dissenting view and consider it.
reversed.self: You are arguing yourself out of a feeling that has something legitimate to tell you.
reversed.advice: Ask someone who disagrees with you to explain their view, and repeat it back before replying.

element.name: Air of Air
element.gloss: Air twice over: thought at its clearest, coolest and most impartial.

astrology.name: Aquarius
astrology.gloss: Aquarius gives him principle and detachment, with concern for what is fair to everyone.

number.name: King
number.gloss: The King rules the suit's domain, turning ideas into judgements that carry weight.

questions: Which decision in your life needs a cooler head and clearer principles?
How do you keep your reasoning honest when the answer affects you personally?

name: Ace of Pentacles
essence: A solid coin in an open palm, and a gate standing ajar.
figure: A hand in an embroidered sleeve reaches from a cloud, holding out a large golden coin stamped with a star. Below it a stone arch smothered in white flowers frames an open iron gate and a path running on toward a distant house. It stands for a tangible opportunity: something real that you can build on.

symbols.meaning: Something concrete on offer: a resource, a chance or a skill with real-world weight.
An invitation to walk through; the way to something lasting is unlocked.
Prosperity as a living thing that blooms where it is looked after.
A long, walkable road toward security, covered one practical step at a time.

upright.short: A practical opportunity needs tending; begin with a concrete, manageable investment of effort.
upright.meaning: The Ace of Pentacles offers a practical beginning. A job, a project, a healthier habit or a useful chance has appeared, and it is solid enough to build on. The card favours treating it like a seed: plant it carefully, give it regular attention and expect growth to come gradually, by steady effort.
upright.love: A relationship gains from practical care: turning up, making plans, doing what you said.
upright.work: A promising opening is in front of you; take the first concrete step to secure it.
upright.self: Start one grounded habit that supports your body or your daily life.
upright.advice: Choose one opportunity and give it a specific, scheduled hour of effort this week.

reversed.short: An opening needs firmer ground; check the plan before it slips away untended.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the coin is offered and the hand hesitates. An opportunity may be slipping past for want of attention, or a start has been made without enough groundwork to hold it up. Sometimes the timing or the terms are simply wrong. A second look at the practical details shows whether to plant or to pass.
reversed.love: Good intentions are not being matched by practical follow-through; make one small promise and keep it.
reversed.work: The plan has a weak foundation; shore up the basics before you add anything on top.
reversed.self: You keep meaning to begin the healthier routine; make the first step almost too easy to skip.
reversed.advice: Look hard at one opportunity and decide plainly: commit to it properly, or let it go.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is the body, work and material life; this card is its first firm foothold.

astrology.name: Earth signs
astrology.gloss: Aces hold the whole element: Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn as a single solid seed.

number.gloss: One is the seed coin, the single stake from which everything else can grow.

questions: What practical opportunity is in front of you that deserves a real first step?
What would you plant today if you trusted yourself to tend it?

name: Two of Pentacles
essence: Two coins in the air, feet dancing on wet rock.
figure: A barefoot dancer balances on the rocks of a wave-beaten shore, tossing two golden coins that are joined by a ribbon looping in a figure of eight, red scarf flying and a smile on her face. She stands for adaptability: keeping several demands in motion with rhythm and good humour.

symbols.meaning: A figure of eight: constant flow between two things, balance achieved by keeping moving.
Competing demands such as time and energy, or work and home, both needing attention.
Changing conditions in the background; the footing has to keep adjusting.
Lightness under pressure, which turns juggling into something nearer play.

upright.short: Balance changing demands flexibly and check what your time and energy can actually hold.
upright.meaning: The Two of Pentacles is life as a juggling act. Demands shift, resources stretch and you keep things moving by staying nimble. It favours flexibility, a sense of rhythm and a certain playfulness about the whole business. It also asks for realism, because two hands can manage only so much before something drops.
upright.love: Make room for each other among competing commitments; rhythm matters more than perfect balance.
upright.work: Prioritise and stay adaptable; handle one thing at a time, quickly, instead of everything at once.
upright.self: Notice what your time and energy can truly hold, and be honest about the limit.
upright.advice: Write down everything you are juggling and decide which single item gets today's best attention.

reversed.short: Too much is in the air; choose what to catch and what to put down.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the rhythm breaks. There are more coins than hands, and the strain shows: forgotten tasks, muddled priorities, a sense of always being behind. The solution is seldom to juggle faster. It is to put something down deliberately, tidy what is left and regain a pace you can keep.
reversed.love: Busyness is leaving the relationship with the leftovers; protect a little time that is only yours together.
reversed.work: You are stretched too thin to do anything well; drop or postpone something on purpose.
reversed.self: Feeling permanently behind is a sign of too many commitments, not of too little effort.
reversed.advice: Say no to one new request this week, and take one existing thing off your plate.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is practical life here, kept supple and in motion instead of fixed.

astrology.name: Jupiter in Capricorn
astrology.gloss: Expansion meeting discipline: growth that has to be managed with care and good timing.

number.gloss: Two is the dance between a pair, balance kept by continual small adjustments.

questions: What are you juggling just now, and which of those things matters most?
Where could you bring more lightness to the way you handle competing demands?

name: Three of Pentacles
essence: Three pairs of hands, one piece of work.
figure: In a stone hall, three craftspeople work side by side: one drives a chisel, one holds up a drawn plan and one kneels to carve a great block, while three golden coins are set in the arch above them. They stand for collaboration and craft, where different skills combine to build something that will last.

symbols.meaning: A shared design; everyone can see what is being built and how the parts fit.
Skill applied by hand, the patient labour that turns a plan into a real thing.
Different roles of equal worth: the one who designs, the one who shapes, the one who finishes.
Value built into the structure itself, the reward of work done well together.

upright.short: Different skills strengthen shared work; ask for useful feedback and give others credit.
upright.meaning: The Three of Pentacles is good work done in company. Each person brings a different ability, and the result is better than any of them could manage alone. It favours planning together, respecting expertise and welcoming feedback. Credit is shared here, and so is the pride of making something well.
upright.love: Build your life together as a joint project, each contributing what you do best.
upright.work: Collaborate, ask for input and acknowledge the skills of the people beside you.
upright.self: Let someone who is good at what you are learning show you how they do it.
upright.advice: Ask for specific feedback on one piece of your work, and thank whoever gives it.

reversed.short: Skills are pulling apart; ask for the feedback you avoid and share the credit.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the workers have stopped consulting the plan. People pull in different directions, feedback is ignored or withheld, and effort is duplicated or wasted. You may be going it alone when the task needs a team, or feeling that your skill goes unrecognised. Agreeing the design again brings the hands back together.
reversed.love: You are working on the relationship separately instead of together; compare your blueprints.
reversed.work: Roles are unclear and standards uneven; clarify who is doing what and to what quality.
reversed.self: Refusing help in order to prove yourself is making the work harder than it needs to be.
reversed.advice: Ask a collaborator, 'What is one thing I could do that would make your part easier?'

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is craft and building here, material shaped by skilled and patient hands.

astrology.name: Mars in Capricorn
astrology.gloss: Driven energy in a disciplined sign: ambition expressed through hard, skilful work.

number.gloss: Three is the first completed structure, something built when separate parts join.

questions: Whose skills complement your own, and how could you work with them more closely?
What feedback have you been avoiding that could improve your work?

name: Four of Pentacles
essence: Four coins held very tight, and a city left unvisited.
figure: A figure sits squarely on a stone bench with eyes closed, arms wrapped around one golden coin, another balanced on the head and one pinned beneath each boot, while a lively domed city spreads out behind, unnoticed. They stand for security and control, and the cost of holding on too tightly.

symbols.meaning: What you clutch to feel safe, held so close that it cannot be used or shared.
Standing on what you have; so fixed in place that taking a step would mean letting go.
Attention narrowed to guarding, with no view of what is going on around you.
Life, exchange and possibility carrying on within reach, kept at a distance.

upright.short: Security matters, but holding too tightly can limit generosity and room to grow.
upright.meaning: The Four of Pentacles is about holding on. Protecting what you have built is sensible, and this card respects prudence and firm boundaries. It also shows the point at which caution becomes a cage. When everything is gripped, nothing can move, grow or be enjoyed. The question is how much holding is enough.
upright.love: Guarding your heart or your independence too closely leaves little room for closeness to enter.
upright.work: Protect what works, and stay open to change; rigid control can stifle the thing you are guarding.
upright.self: Notice what you grip out of worry, and whether a looser hold would really be unsafe.
upright.advice: Loosen your grip on one small thing today: share it, use it or let someone else hold it.

reversed.short: Notice where a tight grip is loosening, or where letting go has gone too far.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the arms begin to open. You may be relaxing a tight hold on resources, plans or people, and finding relief in that. Or the grip has given way too suddenly and things are slipping through your fingers. Somewhere between clutching and carelessness lies a secure, generous middle to aim for.
reversed.love: You are learning to trust instead of control; let a partner in a little further.
reversed.work: Sharing information, credit or responsibility strengthens what you have built.
reversed.self: A sense of scarcity has been steering you; question whether it matches your actual circumstances.
reversed.advice: Give something away this week, whether time, help or an object, and notice how it feels.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is possession here, what is owned and held, heavy enough to weigh you down.

astrology.name: Sun in Capricorn
astrology.gloss: Steady ambition in a careful sign: achievement that wants to be kept and protected.

number.gloss: Four is the closed square, a stable form that can turn into a locked box.

questions: What are you holding on to tightly, and what do you believe would happen if you loosened your hold?
Where does your caution protect you, and where does it merely confine you?

name: Five of Pentacles
essence: Snow outside, and a lit door standing open.
figure: Two travellers wrapped in worn cloaks make their way through falling snow, one leaning on a stick, past a stone building whose stained-glass window shows five golden coins. Just ahead a door stands open, warm light spilling out, and someone waits there to welcome them in. They stand for hardship, and the help that is closer than it feels.

symbols.meaning: Support that is available and already being offered, a short step from where you stand.
Warmth and resources visible nearby, a reminder that you are not as far out as it seems.
Company in a hard season; difficulty shared is difficulty halved.
A lean, cold stretch that is real and also seasonal; winters pass.
Making do and keeping going, with whatever support is to hand.

upright.short: A sense of scarcity or exclusion invites practical support; you do not have to manage alone.
upright.meaning: The Five of Pentacles shows a difficult patch: money, health, belonging or energy running short, and a feeling of being out in the cold. It treats that struggle with respect. The card's emphasis is on the open door. Help exists, and reaching for it is an act of good sense and courage, never a failure.
upright.love: Lean on each other through a hard spell; saying 'I am struggling' invites closeness.
upright.work: Resources are tight or you feel overlooked; ask plainly for the support or information you need.
upright.self: You do not have to manage this alone; let one person know how things really are.
upright.advice: Name one source of help you have not yet tried, and take a first step toward it today.

reversed.short: Support is nearer than it looks; accept the open door and take one step inside.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the travellers reach the doorway. A lean season begins to ease, help is accepted and a sense of belonging returns. Recovery may be gradual. The card can also point to an old belief that you must cope alone, which lingers after conditions have improved; you are allowed to come in and get warm.
reversed.love: Pride is giving way, and you can let someone look after you for once.
reversed.work: Things are improving; rebuild steadily and remember who offered a hand.
reversed.self: The habit of expecting scarcity can outlast the scarcity itself; notice what you do have.
reversed.advice: Accept the next sincere offer of help without apologising or keeping count.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is material need here: the body's requirement for warmth, shelter and care.

astrology.name: Mercury in Taurus
astrology.gloss: Practical thinking in a sign of comfort: the mind preoccupied with security and need.

number.gloss: Five shakes the stable four, a rough patch that tests what you rely on.

questions: Where is the open door in your situation, and what keeps you from walking through it?
Who would want to know that you are having a hard time?

name: Six of Pentacles
essence: A coin given, a scale held, and questions about both.
figure: A robed merchant holds a pair of golden scales in one hand and with the other places a coin into the cupped palms of an older man, while a woman in a red headscarf waits beside him with open hands and five more coins hang overhead. They stand for generosity and exchange, and the balance of power within giving.

symbols.meaning: Fairness being measured; how much is given, to whom, and on what terms.
Help in its most concrete form: resources moving from where they are to where they are needed.
The courage it takes to receive, and the vulnerability of having to ask.
The difference in power that comes with every gift, to be handled with care.

upright.short: Notice the balance of giving and receiving, including the power attached to an offer.
upright.meaning: The Six of Pentacles is about resources flowing between people. You may be the one who gives, the one who receives, or both in different parts of your life. The card favours generosity that respects the other person's dignity, and receiving without shame. It also asks who holds the scales and whether they are level.
upright.love: Check that care flows in both directions, and that neither of you is always the giver.
upright.work: Share knowledge, credit or opportunity generously; accept mentoring where it is offered.
upright.self: Notice whether you find it easier to give or to receive, and practise the harder one.
upright.advice: Give something freely today, or ask for something you need, whichever you find more difficult.

reversed.short: Look at whether giving comes with strings, or receiving has become one-sided.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the scales dip. Generosity may come with conditions, or one person gives constantly while the other only takes. You could be overextending yourself to be needed, or feeling beholden to somebody's favours. A fair exchange leaves both people freer. Naming the imbalance is how it starts to correct.
reversed.love: One of you keeps a tally, or one of you does all the giving; bring it into the open.
reversed.work: Help is being offered with an agenda, or your effort is not being fairly returned.
reversed.self: Giving until you are empty is not generosity; include yourself among those you look after.
reversed.advice: Before you offer or accept help, ask honestly what each side expects in return.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is shared resources here, the practical business of distributing what there is.

astrology.name: Moon in Taurus
astrology.gloss: Caring instinct in a sign of plenty: the comfort of providing and of being provided for.

number.gloss: Six is reciprocity, harmony restored through balanced giving and receiving.

questions: Do you find it harder to give or to receive, and what does that tell you?
Where in your life is an exchange out of balance, and what would make it fair?

name: Seven of Pentacles
essence: Leaning on the hoe, sizing up the vine.
figure: A gardener leans on the handle of a hoe, chin resting on folded hands, and gazes thoughtfully at a tall vine on which seven golden coins have grown among the leaves. The work is paused and far from finished. They stand for patience and assessment: the long middle of an effort that is slowly bearing fruit.

symbols.meaning: Results of sustained effort, visible and growing, though not yet ready for harvest.
The tool of ongoing work, set down for a moment and not put away.
A pause for evaluation; stepping back to see what the labour has produced.
Boundaries set long ago that have given this growth a sheltered place.

upright.short: Pause to review a slow-growing effort; decide what deserves continued care or adjustment.
upright.meaning: The Seven of Pentacles is a pause to see where things stand. You have put in real work and the results are coming, slowly. The card favours stepping back to review: what is growing well, what needs a different approach and whether this is still the right vine to tend. Patience here is active and observant.
upright.love: A relationship grows by steady tending; reflect on what you have built and what it needs next.
upright.work: Review progress on the long project and adjust the plan in light of what is actually working.
upright.self: Give yourself credit for slow, unglamorous progress; it is the kind that tends to last.
upright.advice: Set aside half an hour to review one long-term effort and decide on a single adjustment.

reversed.short: Effort and reward feel out of step; review what you tend before working harder.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the gardener frowns at the vine. A great deal of work seems to have produced very little, and impatience or discouragement sets in. You may be tending the wrong plant, or simply expecting fruit too early. An honest review, without self-blame, shows whether to persist, prune or replant elsewhere.
reversed.love: You are putting in effort that goes unreturned; raise it instead of quietly trying harder.
reversed.work: Results do not match the hours going in; reassess before you add more.
reversed.self: Frustration at slow progress is tempting you to give up just before the growth shows.
reversed.advice: Ask of one ongoing effort: is this worth another season, and what would have to change?

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is slow cultivation here, growth that keeps to the soil's own schedule.

astrology.name: Saturn in Taurus
astrology.gloss: Patience and time in a sign of steady growth: rewards that come only by waiting and working.

number.gloss: Seven is the pause to assess, a testing interval between the planting and the harvest.

questions: Which long-term effort deserves a patient review instead of a hasty verdict?
What are you cultivating that is growing more than you have noticed?

name: Eight of Pentacles
essence: One more coin on the bench, cut a little truer than the last.
figure: A craftsperson in an apron bends over a workbench, carefully cutting a star into a golden disc with a fine chisel, while seven finished coins line the shelves behind and shavings curl across the table. They are wholly absorbed. They stand for diligence and apprenticeship: skill built through repetition and care.

symbols.meaning: The present piece of work, receiving complete attention regardless of how many came before.
A record of practice; each earlier attempt taught something used in the next.
Precision and the right tool, mastery found in small exact movements.
The by-product of real effort, evidence that work is actually being done.

upright.short: Patient practice builds skill; improve one small detail rather than chasing instant mastery.
upright.meaning: The Eight of Pentacles is the satisfaction of getting better at something. It favours focused, repeated practice and pride in the detail. No shortcut is on offer and none is needed. Each coin is a little finer than the last, and the steady rhythm of the work becomes rewarding in its own right.
upright.love: Relationships improve with practice too: small, consistent efforts to listen and show care.
upright.work: Hone your craft; take on the training, refine the detail and let quality speak for you.
upright.self: Choose a skill you want and practise it regularly, enjoying the gradual improvement.
upright.advice: Spend a focused half hour on deliberate practice of one skill, with distractions put away.

reversed.short: Notice where practice has become perfectionism, or effort is spent without care.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the chisel slips or will not stop. Work has become joyless repetition, or perfectionism keeps you polishing something that is already good enough. The opposite also shows up as rushed, careless effort. Reconnecting with why this skill matters to you restores both the care and the sense of proportion.
reversed.love: Effort has become dutiful instead of heartfelt; do one thing for love and not from routine.
reversed.work: You are either over-polishing or coasting; ask what standard this task actually requires.
reversed.self: Working hard at something you no longer care about is a kind of drift; check your direction.
reversed.advice: Declare one thing finished at 'good enough' and move on to what matters next.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is skilled labour here, the hands learning what the head already knows.

astrology.name: Sun in Virgo
astrology.gloss: Vitality in a meticulous sign: finding purpose in careful, useful and well-made work.

number.gloss: Eight is repetition with purpose, the steady rhythm through which mastery is built.

questions: Which skill would you be glad to have spent a year practising?
Where could a little more care, or a little less perfectionism, improve your work?

name: Nine of Pentacles
essence: A garden of your own making, enjoyed at leisure.
figure: A woman in a flowered gown sits at ease among vines heavy with grapes and nine golden coins, a hooded falcon perched calmly on her gloved hand, with a villa on the green hillside behind her. She is alone and entirely content. She stands for self-sufficiency: comfort earned by one's own effort and enjoyed without apology.

symbols.meaning: Discipline and trained instinct; a wild thing that stays through patience and mutual respect.
Ripeness after long cultivation, plenty that came from her own tending.
Self-control worn lightly, and the skill to handle power without being scratched by it.
A settled, well-kept life, the visible outcome of sound choices over time.

upright.short: Enjoy a hard-earned measure of independence and the everyday pleasures it makes possible.
upright.meaning: The Nine of Pentacles shows the pleasures of a life you have built for yourself. It favours enjoying what your discipline has made possible: comfort, beauty, time and the freedom to choose. There is quiet pride here and no need for an audience. Solitude in this garden is a luxury, not a lack.
upright.love: Being content on your own makes you a freer and more generous partner.
upright.work: Your effort has earned you some independence; enjoy it and use it deliberately.
upright.self: Treat yourself well as a matter of course, and take pleasure in your own company.
upright.advice: Spend an hour enjoying something you worked for, without multitasking or guilt.

reversed.short: Ask whether self-reliance has become isolation, or comfort is covering a restlessness.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the garden wall feels high. Independence may have tipped into keeping everyone out, or you are working so hard for comfort that you never sit down in it. It can also show reliance on someone else's resources that leaves your own footing unsure. Ask what self-sufficiency would mean for you now.
reversed.love: Self-reliance has become a wall; letting someone help does not diminish what you have built.
reversed.work: You have earned the reward and are not letting yourself enjoy it; pause before the next target.
reversed.self: Your worth is not the same as your productivity or your possessions.
reversed.advice: Either invite someone into your garden this week, or sit in it properly yourself.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is cultivated abundance here, nature shaped by discipline into something gracious.

astrology.name: Venus in Virgo
astrology.gloss: Pleasure in a discerning sign: enjoyment that is refined, selective and well deserved.

number.gloss: Nine is personal attainment, the harvest one person gathers from their own work.

questions: What have you built for yourself that you seldom stop to enjoy?
Where does your independence serve you, and where does it keep others at a distance?

name: Ten of Pentacles
essence: Three generations, two dogs and an arch that lasts.
figure: Under a stone arch set with ten golden coins and wreathed in flowers, a family gathers: grey-haired elders, parents and a laughing child, with two dogs at their feet and a tiled villa behind. They stand for legacy and lasting security, the wealth of belonging to something that outlives any one person.

symbols.meaning: A lasting structure that shelters everyone beneath it, built to be handed on.
Continuity; what one generation plants, another tends and a third enjoys.
Loyalty and the comfort of home, companions who belong to the whole household.
An established home, stability made from many years of ordinary care.

upright.short: Consider the lasting structures, shared resources and traditions you want to pass on.
upright.meaning: The Ten of Pentacles is about what endures. It shows security built over time and shared across generations: a home, a family, a tradition or a body of work. The card favours thinking in the long term, valuing your roots and considering what you are building for those who come after you.
upright.love: Think about the life you are building together over years, including the traditions you want.
upright.work: Contribute to something lasting; put your effort where it keeps building over time.
upright.self: Consider what you have inherited, in every sense, and what you would like to pass on.
upright.advice: Do one thing today that your future self, or those who follow you, would thank you for.

reversed.short: Look at what you inherited, in habits as well as resources, and what to pass on.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the arch shows a crack. There may be friction over family expectations, shared resources or a tradition that no longer fits. Stability can feel like obligation. You might be carrying an inheritance, material or emotional, that you never chose. Deciding consciously what to keep and what to end is the work here.
reversed.love: Family expectations are pressing on the relationship; agree which ones to honour.
reversed.work: Short-term gain is winning out over lasting value; step back and take the longer view.
reversed.self: You are free to keep the best of where you come from and to lay down the rest.
reversed.advice: Identify one inherited habit or expectation and decide whether you want to continue it.

element.name: Earth
element.gloss: Earth is rootedness here, the deep ground of home, lineage and lasting things.

astrology.name: Mercury in Virgo
astrology.gloss: Careful thought at home in its own sign: planning and stewardship done thoroughly.

number.gloss: Ten is fullness, the suit's material security complete and ready to be handed on.

questions: What do you want to pass on, and to whom?
Which inherited tradition do you treasure, and which would you gently retire?

name: Page of Pentacles
essence: A coin held to the chest like a promise.
figure: A young person stands in a meadow thick with wildflowers, holding a golden coin against their chest with both hands and looking up toward the sky, a leather satchel at their hip and snowy mountains behind. They stand for the diligent student: someone with a practical dream who is ready to learn how to make it real.

symbols.meaning: A goal treated as precious, studied and kept near before it is spent or risked.
Aspiration: the dream is practical, and the eyes are still raised toward what could be.
Fertile ground and fresh possibility; an ideal place to plant something.
A student's bag, room for tools and notes and whatever is learned on the way.

upright.short: Approach a practical skill with curiosity and turn an intention into a learnable first task.
upright.meaning: The Page of Pentacles is ready to learn. A goal has taken shape: a skill, a qualification, a venture or a better habit, and the first step is to study it properly. The card favours patience, curiosity and small real actions. Ambition here is modest and serious, the kind that turns up on time and takes notes.
upright.love: Show interest through reliability and thoughtful attention; steady effort is its own romance.
upright.work: Take the course, shadow the expert or start the entry-level version; learn by doing.
upright.self: Pick something practical you want to improve and commit to being its student.
upright.advice: Turn one intention into a first task small enough to complete in a single sitting.

reversed.short: A practical intention is drifting; choose one learnable task and begin it.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the coin is studied and never spent. Plans stay theoretical, attention wanders or you lose heart when learning proves slower than you hoped. There may be many intentions and little follow-through. Bringing the goal down to one small, learnable task turns daydreaming back into progress.
reversed.love: Meaning well is not reaching the other person; let your care show in some practical act.
reversed.work: You are putting off the dull foundations; do the basics first and the interesting part follows.
reversed.self: Waiting until you feel ready is keeping you a spectator of your own plans.
reversed.advice: Choose the smallest possible version of your goal and do it before the day is out.

element.name: Earth of Earth
element.gloss: Earth doubled: the most grounded of the pages, learning by handling real things.

astrology.name: Earth signs
astrology.gloss: Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn share this card, each lending the learner some patience.

number.name: Page
number.gloss: The Page is the learner, approaching the suit's practical world with respect and care.

questions: What practical skill would you like to be learning, and what would the first lesson be?
Which of your intentions is ready to become a small, concrete task?

name: Knight of Pentacles
essence: A still horse, a studied coin and no hurry at all.
figure: A rider in dark, well-kept gear sits a black horse that stands perfectly still in a green field, holding up a single golden coin and considering it, with a farmhouse and cypress trees in the distance. Nothing here is rushed. The rider stands for reliability: methodical effort that reaches the end because it never stops.

symbols.meaning: Patience and stamina; progress comes from consistency, not speed.
The goal kept squarely in view and weighed with care before each step.
Work already done and waiting to be continued, row by patient row.
The plain, solid destination: security built through routine.

upright.short: Steady, dependable action can carry a plan forward; watch for routine becoming rigidity.
upright.meaning: The Knight of Pentacles gets there by not stopping. This card favours method, routine and seeing things through to the end. It lacks glamour and is deeply trustworthy. Its shadow is plodding: a path followed so faithfully that you forget to look up and check whether it still leads somewhere you want to be.
upright.love: Be dependable: keep your promises, turn up, and let trust build through consistency.
upright.work: Work through the task methodically and finish what you start; thoroughness wins here.
upright.self: Lean on routine; a few steady daily habits can carry you a long way.
upright.advice: Choose one task and take it through to completion today, however unexciting.

reversed.short: Check whether routine has become a rut, or steadiness has stalled into delay.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the horse will not move or the rider has nodded off in the saddle. Routine has turned into a rut, caution into inertia, and thoroughness into refusing to adapt. The reverse can also be true: steadiness abandoned for carelessness. Shaking up one habit, or recommitting to a dropped one, gets things moving again.
reversed.love: Predictability has slid into taking each other for granted; add something unexpected.
reversed.work: You are stuck in a process that no longer makes sense; propose an improvement.
reversed.self: Dull routine is draining you; change one element and see whether your energy shifts.
reversed.advice: Do one regular task differently today, or restart one useful habit you let lapse.

element.name: Fire of Earth
element.gloss: Fire banked in earth: a slow, steady burn that powers long practical work.

astrology.name: Virgo
astrology.gloss: Virgo makes this knight careful, hard-working and attentive to getting the details right.

number.name: Knight
number.gloss: The Knight carries the suit forward, here at a walking pace that never falters.

questions: Where would steady, unglamorous consistency serve you better than a burst of effort?
Which of your routines supports you, and which have you simply stopped questioning?

name: Queen of Pentacles
essence: A warm kitchen, a tended garden, a coin kept in the lap.
figure: A queen crowned with leaves and flowers sits on a carved garden throne in a floral robe, one hand resting on a golden coin in her lap, a rabbit at her side and pots of flowers, grapes and roses crowding around. She stands for practical nurture: generosity that shows itself in comfort, resourcefulness and care.

symbols.meaning: Resources held comfortably and close, managed with care and ready to be put to use.
Fertility and gentleness; small living things thrive in the shelter she provides.
Deliberate tending; even the wild is given a container and regular water.
Authority rooted in home ground, her seat placed among what she has grown.

upright.short: Make care tangible through comfort, resourcefulness and a sustainable daily rhythm.
upright.meaning: The Queen of Pentacles makes life feel good in tangible ways. She favours looking after the body, the home and the people in it with warmth and good sense: a meal cooked, a budget minded, a room made welcoming. Her care sustains because it includes herself and follows a rhythm she can keep.
upright.love: Show love in practical forms: comfort, thoughtfulness and a welcoming home.
upright.work: Manage resources sensibly and look after the people you work with; both pay off.
upright.self: Tend your own wellbeing through simple, regular comforts and a daily rhythm you can sustain.
upright.advice: Make one corner of your home or one meal a little more nourishing than usual today.

reversed.short: Notice where caring for everything else has left your own comfort untended.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the garden is flourishing and the gardener is exhausted. You may be so busy looking after others, or managing practical demands, that your own needs fall away. Care can also tip into fussing, or comfort into fixation on things. Restoring your own daily rhythm puts the warmth back into your giving.
reversed.love: Mothering a partner, or being mothered, is unbalancing things; step back into an equal footing.
reversed.work: Home and work are competing and you are the one squeezed; protect a boundary on each side.
reversed.self: You look after everything except yourself; put your own needs on the list in ink.
reversed.advice: Schedule one act of practical self-care this week and treat it as non-negotiable.

element.name: Water of Earth
element.gloss: Water within earth: practical life softened by tenderness, like rain on a garden.

astrology.name: Capricorn
astrology.gloss: Capricorn gives her competence and stamina, a quiet mastery of the material world.

number.name: Queen
number.gloss: The Queen embodies the suit from within, turning resources into wellbeing.

questions: How do you make care tangible for the people you love, and for yourself?
What would a sustainable daily rhythm look like for you at present?

name: King of Pentacles
essence: Plenty, managed well and shared widely.
figure: A grey-bearded king, crowned and wrapped in embroidered velvet, leans back in a stone chair with a bull's head cut into its side, a golden coin balanced on his knee, grapes ripening at his feet and vineyards and a villa stretching out behind him. He stands for stewardship: prosperity built with patience and used responsibly.

symbols.meaning: Strength, steadiness and endurance, the solid foundation on which his success rests.
Wealth held with a relaxed hand, neither flaunted nor clutched.
Abundance that comes of long cultivation and is there to be shared.
An estate that supports many people; his prosperity is a responsibility.

upright.short: Steward resources responsibly and use stability to support people as well as achievement.
upright.meaning: The King of Pentacles has built something solid and knows how to look after it. He favours long-term thinking, prudent management and generosity grounded in stability. Success here is measured by what it supports: people, projects and community. He provides, he is dependable, and he enjoys the fruits of his work.
upright.love: Offer stability, generosity and a steady presence; be someone who can be counted on.
upright.work: Lead with practical wisdom; manage resources responsibly and back your people.
upright.self: Acknowledge what you have built, and use your stability to support what you value.
upright.advice: Use something you have in plenty, whether time, skill or resources, to help someone today.

reversed.short: Ask whether stability serves people, or status and control have become the goal.
reversed.meaning: Reversed, the coin has grown heavier than the people around it. Success turns into accumulation for its own sake, generosity into control, or caution into stubborn refusal to change. It can also show resources poorly managed. The correction is to remember what prosperity is for, and whom it is meant to serve.
reversed.love: Providing materially is standing in for emotional presence; offer your time as well.
reversed.work: Fixation on the bottom line is costing loyalty and goodwill; weigh the human factors.
reversed.self: You are measuring your worth by what you own or earn; widen the definition.
reversed.advice: Ask whether one of your resources is serving people or merely piling up, and redirect it.

element.name: Air of Earth
element.gloss: Air applied to earth: material life steered by planning and long foresight.

astrology.name: Taurus
astrology.gloss: Taurus gives him patience, a love of good things and a talent for making them last.

number.name: King
number.gloss: As King he answers for the suit's results and for the prosperity of those who rely on him.

questions: What have you built that could now support someone other than yourself?
How do you measure success, and does that measure still fit who you are?
